title: Project-path launcher over-excludes .coder and loses active mode state
description:
## Description
Discovered while verifying `opencode-coder-lg2.6`.

## Precise problem
This is a **test harness bug** in the manual launcher copy workflow, not a product bug.

While fixing `opencode-coder-4yl`, the harness added `.coder` to `EXCLUDED_COPY_SEGMENTS` in `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts`.
That exclusion is too broad.

`.coder/` contains both:
- transient runtime files such as `project.yaml`
- the **persisted active-mode marker** `.coder/opencode-coder.yaml`

When `--project-path` copies a prepared active project into an isolated workspace, excluding the entire `.coder/` directory removes the canonical mode state file. The copied project is then reclassified as `not-enabled` / `fresh`, so active docs lifecycle scenarios cannot be verified.

## Root cause hypothesis
Current exclusion logic treats `.coder/` as fully transient. That is incorrect.

- `.beads/` should stay excluded (socket/state/logs)
- `.coder/opencode-coder.yaml` must be preserved for active mode detection
- `.coder/project.yaml` and runtime logs can still be excluded as transient

## Why this matters
This blocks acceptance scenarios A/B/C in `opencode-coder-lg2.6` because the documented `--project-path` manual workflow cannot preserve prepared team/stealth mode into the isolated workspace.

## Recommended fix direction
- remove `.coder` from the global excluded segment list
- keep excluding `.git` and `.beads`
- add more specific path-level exclusions for transient `.coder` artifacts only (for example `project.yaml`, logs, or other runtime-only files)
- add regression coverage that a copied prepared project retains the same active mode as the source

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Manual launcher `--project-path` preserves `.coder/opencode-coder.yaml`
- [ ] Copied prepared team/stealth projects resolve to the same active mode as the source project
- [ ] Transient `.coder` runtime files remain excluded where appropriate
- [ ] Regression coverage proves mode state survives project-path copy
close_reason: Fixed manual launcher project-path copy filtering: preserve .coder/opencode-coder.yaml for saved mode state, exclude transient .coder/project.yaml and .coder/logs, and added regression assertions in manual-launcher e2e test for mode preservation.

title: E2E real-server existing active project omits docs lifecycle commands
description:
Discovered while re-verifying opencode-coder-lg2.6.

- Received command list: `["init", "review", "opencode-coder/init"]`

Artifact: `tests/e2e/.artifacts/scenario-1-existing-real-server-startup/notes.txt`

This blocks acceptance for opencode-coder-lg2.6 because:

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Gate docs lifecycle commands on runtime resource availability
description:
## Description
Fix the root runtime contract bug behind the failed docs lifecycle acceptance review: the plugin currently exposes `/opencode-coder/docs` and `/opencode-coder/improve-doc` before the required runtime resources are actually available.

## Why
This is the shared root cause behind the acceptance failures around `/opencode-coder/docs`. If command exposure is wrong, functional verification and later init behavior become unreliable.

## Related Bugs
- `opencode-coder-gq1`
- partially addresses the automated-coverage side of `opencode-coder-e3v`

## Instructions
1. In the runtime plugin registration path, decide and implement the resource-availability contract for docs lifecycle commands.
2. Recommended behavior:
   - do **not** expose `/opencode-coder/docs` or `/opencode-coder/improve-doc` unless the required runtime resources are actually available
3. If you choose a different behavior (for example exposed-with-helpful-error), it must be explicit, deterministic, and covered by tests.
4. Update integration tests so command exposure is correct across:
   - fresh inactive
   - saved disabled
   - active team
   - active stealth
5. Update any unit/e2e contract tests needed so the runtime command set matches the intended model.
6. Keep the fix focused on the runtime exposure contract; do not mix in the init template fix here.

## Files to Modify
- `src/index.ts`
- `tests/integration/plugin.test.ts`
- `tests/unit/docs-lifecycle-contract.test.ts` (if needed)
- `tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts` (if needed)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Docs lifecycle commands are not exposed before their required runtime resources are available, or an explicitly tested graceful fallback is implemented
- [ ] Integration tests cover command exposure/removal across inactive, disabled, team, and stealth modes
- [ ] Runtime command exposure no longer leads to the verifier reproduction failure from `opencode-coder-gq1`
- [ ] Relevant tests pass
close_reason: Implemented runtime gating so docs lifecycle commands are only exposed when runtime resources are available, with integration coverage across inactive/disabled/team/stealth modes.

title: Runtime /opencode-coder/init is missing the docs lifecycle step
description:
## Description
Discovered while verifying `opencode-coder-lg2.6`.

## What failed
The actual runtime `/opencode-coder/init` command registered by the plugin does not include the optional project-doc setup/refresh step required by the acceptance task.

## Evidence
- Runtime registration comes from `src/index.ts` via `getInstallGuideTemplate()`
- `src/templates/init-install-guide.ts` still ends at AGENTS generation + completion reporting
- It does not mention:
  - `Set up project docs now` / `Skip for now`
  - `references/project-docs-lifecycle.md`
  - `references/project-setup.md`
  - topic decision matrix
  - created/updated/skipped/routed docs reporting
- The published file `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md` includes that docs step, so runtime behavior and published guidance have drifted apart

## Important implementation note
The fix is **not** to blindly copy the published command file into the runtime template.

The runtime template still needs to be safe when skill/resources are unavailable. The correct fix is a **conditional docs lifecycle step** that is shown only when the runtime can actually support it.

## Why this matters
Acceptance criterion 2 requires that `/opencode-coder/init` can optionally guide docs setup using the shared lifecycle reference. The shipped runtime command does not currently do that.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The runtime init template includes the optional docs lifecycle step when the runtime can support it
- [ ] The runtime template remains safe/self-consistent when docs lifecycle resources are unavailable
- [ ] The init template references the same lifecycle model used by the docs command rather than inventing a separate one
- [ ] Any unit or guide-contract tests needed for the updated init text are added or updated
close_reason: Fixed by opencode-coder-a82: runtime init template now includes conditional docs lifecycle follow-through with unit coverage for available/unavailable paths.

title: Runtime /opencode-coder/docs is exposed before its skill/reference dependencies are available
description:
## Description
Discovered while verifying `opencode-coder-lg2.6`.

## Root problem
The plugin exposes `/opencode-coder/docs` while its required published skill/reference resources may be unavailable or unresolved in the runtime execution context.

## What failed
Executing `/opencode-coder/docs` in the documented isolated manual/e2e-style environment failed because the command relied on skill/reference resources that were not available through the runtime context.

## Correct evidence
Manual reproduction command:
- `bun run test:manual -- --mode=command --fixture=existing-active-project --keep -- opencode run --command "opencode-coder/docs"`

Observed stderr:
- `Error: Skill "opencode-coder" not found. Available skills: none`
- `Error: File not found: /tmp/.../project/references/project-structure.md`
- `Error: File not found: /tmp/.../project/references/project-docs-lifecycle.md`

Result:
- command exposure succeeded
- functional execution failed in isolated runtime
- process eventually timed out

## Why this matters
Acceptance scenarios A/B require actually running `/opencode-coder/docs`. Today the command can be exposed while the resources it depends on are unavailable.

## Implementation direction
Fix the resource-gating model before anything else:
- either gate `/opencode-coder/docs` and `/opencode-coder/improve-doc` on resource availability, or
- provide a graceful fallback path that does not depend on missing published skill resources

Recommended default: do **not** expose the docs lifecycle commands unless their required resources are actually available.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The plugin does not expose docs lifecycle commands when their required runtime resources are unavailable
- [ ] Or, if commands remain exposed, they fail gracefully with an explicit, actionable message instead of timing out
- [ ] Integration tests cover inactive/disabled/team/stealth command exposure correctly
- [ ] The fix establishes the runtime contract that later tasks and acceptance review can rely on
close_reason: Fixed by opencode-coder-67d: runtime now gates docs lifecycle commands on resource availability and integration coverage verifies the contract across inactive/disabled/team/stealth modes.

title: Add release-grade e2e regression for non-ready startup toast hang
description:
## Description
Add release-grade e2e regression coverage for the historical startup hang in active-but-not-ready projects.

We verified with the installed-vs-local reproduction workflow against `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-orchestrator` that:
- installed `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.34.2` can hang on startup in the active/non-ready path
- current local build no longer shows that hang
- the likely root cause matches the `0.34.3` fix where the readiness toast (`"Orchestrator not enabled"`) no longer blocks the plugin config hook

There is already good mocked integration coverage in `tests/integration/plugin.test.ts` (`does not block config when readiness toast never resolves`), but we do **not** yet have a release-grade e2e guard that exercises a real OpenCode startup path for an explicitly active, non-ready project.

## Why This Task Exists
The current integration test is strong for the exact code path, but it is still mock-based. It does not prove that a real CLI/server startup in an explicitly active but non-ready project will finish instead of blank-screening or hanging.

This task should add a black-box e2e guard on the non-ready active startup path so a future regression in the startup flow is caught before release.

## Important Design Constraints
- Do **not** add a production env-var hook that stalls `showToast()`.
  - The current fix uses `void showToast(...)`, so a stalled toast promise is no longer awaited.
  - A toast-stall env var would therefore be the wrong seam and would create false-confidence coverage.
- Prefer a pure black-box runtime test over new production test hooks.
- Reuse existing fixtures and harness helpers unless a real gap forces a new fixture.

## Instructions
1. Reuse the existing active/non-ready fixture if it already satisfies the scenario.
   - Start by evaluating `tests/e2e/fixtures/existing-active-project/`
   - It already appears to represent an explicitly active (`mode: team`) but non-ready (`ecosystemReady: false`) project baseline
   - Only create a new fixture if the existing one cannot express the scenario cleanly
2. Add a real CLI e2e scenario in `tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts`.
   - Follow the existing scenario-2 style (`opencode run --command "pwd" --format json`)
   - Use the active/non-ready fixture
   - Wire the local built plugin artifact with `wireBuiltPluginArtifact(...)`
   - Create isolated OpenCode paths with the existing harness helpers
   - Use the same timeout discipline as the other CLI smoke scenarios so hangs fail loudly and consistently
3. Assert that the test exercised the correct startup path.
   - Assert the CLI command exits successfully and does not time out
   - Assert `.coder/project.yaml` after startup still reflects a non-ready result (`ecosystemReady: false`)
   - Assert the project remains in active mode (`mode: team`) so the test cannot silently pass through inactive startup behavior
4. If feasible with existing helpers, add one more active-startup proof.
   - Preferred proof: use the existing real-server probe and assert the `coder` tool is present
   - If that proof adds unacceptable runtime or flakiness, document in the test comments why the `project.yaml` assertions are sufficient
5. Keep the existing integration regression test.
   - Do not replace `does not block config when readiness toast never resolves`
   - The new e2e should be additive coverage layered on top of the integration test
6. Update `docs/TESTING.md` only if the new scenario introduces behavior or fixture intent that would otherwise be surprising to future maintainers

## Files to Modify
- `tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts` — add the new active/non-ready startup regression scenario
- `docs/TESTING.md` — update only if needed to explain the scenario or fixture choice
- `tests/e2e/fixtures/existing-active-project/README.md` — update only if needed to clarify that this fixture intentionally represents the active/non-ready regression path

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A real CLI e2e test covers an explicitly active but non-ready startup path
- [ ] The test uses existing fixtures/helpers unless a concrete limitation justifies adding a new fixture
- [ ] The new e2e fails on hang/timeout and passes when startup continues normally
- [ ] The new e2e proves it ran in active mode and ended in a non-ready state
- [ ] The existing integration regression test remains in place
- [ ] Relevant test command(s) pass after implementation
close_reason: Closed by user decision — no longer needed.

title: Installed-configured manual harness does not load configured opencode-coder package
description:
## Description
Discovered while verifying acceptance task `opencode-coder-uwf.4`.

`installed-configured` mode currently exits 0 but does not actually load the configured `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder` package, so installed-vs-local comparison is invalid.

## Root Cause Hypothesis
The current harness relies on OpenCode runtime plugin installation inside a fully isolated HOME/XDG environment. In verification, OpenCode attempted to install the configured package at runtime and failed, leaving the project at `pluginVersion: fixture` while the launcher still looked superficially successful.

## Reproduction
1. Run:
   `bun run test:manual -- --mode=command --project-path "/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder/tests/e2e/fixtures/existing-active-project" --plugin-source=installed-configured --keep -- opencode run --command "pwd" --format json`
2. Inspect the preserved workspace, `.coder/project.yaml`, and isolated OpenCode log.

## Observed
- Launcher exits 0 and prints `Resolved installed package: @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.34.2`
- `Loaded plugin version` remains `fixture`
- `.coder/project.yaml` stays at `pluginVersion: fixture`
- Real-server probe exposes no `coder` tool and no `opencode-coder/init` command
- Isolated OpenCode log shows package-install failure while attempting to load the configured package

## Required Fix
1. Do **not** rely on opaque OpenCode runtime installation for `installed-configured` mode.
2. Pre-install or otherwise prepare the resolved installed package during harness setup in a deterministic way, analogous to how local-build mode prepares the workspace before launch.
3. Make installed-configured setup fail loudly if package preparation/loading cannot succeed.
4. Add concrete post-run detection/guardrails so the launcher cannot report a successful comparison when the installed plugin never loaded.
5. Harden tests and docs so they require real version proof and do not accept `pluginVersion: fixture` as a successful installed-configured run.

## Files Likely In Scope
- `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts`
- `scripts/manual-test/index.ts`
- `tests/e2e/manual-launcher.test.ts`
- `docs/TESTING.md`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Installed-configured mode prepares the resolved plugin package before launch or fails loudly before claiming success
- [ ] Installed-configured runs prove the configured plugin actually loaded (not `fixture`)
- [ ] Launcher emits an explicit invalid-comparison signal when installed plugin loading proof is missing
- [ ] Manual-launcher tests fail if installed-configured mode leaves fixture baseline version markers in place
- [ ] Docs no longer imply installed-vs-local comparison works unless that proof is available
close_reason: Implemented deterministic installed-configured package preparation in harness, added launcher invalid-comparison guardrails with required version proof, and updated tests/docs to reject fixture baseline as success.

title: Installed-vs-local verification lacks concrete version proof and false-success guard
description:
Discovered while verifying acceptance task opencode-coder-uwf.4.

Problem:
- `tests/e2e/manual-launcher.test.ts` only checks that installed-configured mode prints a `Loaded plugin version:` line, not that the version differs from the fixture baseline or that the plugin actually loaded.
- `docs/TESTING.md` currently tells investigators to compare `Plugin source`, `Resolved installed package`, `Loaded plugin version`, and `Configured plugin loading` to confirm a source switch. In practice the installed-configured run can still exit 0 while `Loaded plugin version` is `fixture` and the plugin never loads.

Observed verification evidence:
- Local-build mode rewrote `.coder/project.yaml` to `pluginVersion: 0.34.3`
- Installed-configured mode left `.coder/project.yaml` at `pluginVersion: fixture`
- The current passing manual-launcher test suite did not catch this gap

Expected:
- Acceptance-proof coverage should assert concrete version proof (or equivalent diagnostics) for both modes and fail when installed-configured does not actually load the configured plugin.
- Launcher/docs should not present a successful comparison workflow unless that proof is available.
close_reason: Merged into opencode-coder-uwf.5 after review; version-proof and false-success guard work is now tracked there.

title: Acceptance Review: published opencode-coder docs lifecycle
description:
## Description
Verify that the published opencode-coder resources support the full project-doc lifecycle: setup, generation, maintenance, auditing, slimming, and incident-driven improvement.

## Verification model
This acceptance review must verify both:
1. **structural correctness** of files, commands, and references
2. **functional behavior** in realistic project modes

## Instructions
1. Review the updated published skill references and commands.
2. Verify the project-setup guidance is available in the published opencode-coder skill.
3. Verify `/opencode-coder/init` can optionally lead into doc setup.
4. Verify there is one unified `/opencode-coder/docs` command and one incident-driven `/opencode-coder/improve-doc` command.
5. Verify `update-agent-md` is removed or clearly superseded.
6. Verify `project-docs-lifecycle.md` is the shared lifecycle reference and `agents-md-template.md` is no longer the owner of standalone lifecycle workflow logic.
7. Verify `opencode-coder` is the recommended home for project-doc create/fix/update/audit/slim/improve guidance.
8. Record any remaining gaps as follow-up issues instead of reopening completed work.

## Functional Scenarios To Verify
### Scenario A — Team mode docs lifecycle
- Active team-mode project
- Existing `docs/CODING.md`
- Relevant skills installed for releases and monitoring
- No other standard topic docs yet
- Run `/opencode-coder/docs`
- Verify:
  - root `AGENTS.md` routes release and monitoring topics to skills instead of creating hollow docs
  - existing `docs/CODING.md` is refreshed rather than blindly recreated
  - no hollow docs are created
  - the command reports what it created, updated, skipped, and routed

### Scenario B — Stealth mode docs lifecycle
- Active stealth-mode project
- Team root `AGENTS.md` already exists
- Run `/opencode-coder/docs`
- Verify:
  - only `.coder/AGENTS.md` and `.coder/docs/` paths are written or refreshed
  - root `AGENTS.md` is not overwritten
  - mode-specific path rules are respected throughout the lifecycle

### Scenario C — Init delegates to docs lifecycle
- Fresh project enabled through `/opencode-coder/init`
- User chooses to set up docs now
- Verify init uses the same lifecycle decisions as `/opencode-coder/docs` rather than inventing a separate docs model

### Scenario D — Incident-driven improvement
- Run `/opencode-coder/improve-doc` with failure context such as `forgot to run validate-before-release.sh`
- Verify the workflow identifies the relevant doc/routing/skill gap and proposes updates aimed at preventing recurrence

### Scenario E — Automated command registration coverage
- Verify automated tests cover:
  - inactive/disabled mode -> init only
  - active team mode -> docs lifecycle commands available
  - active stealth mode -> docs lifecycle commands available
  - `update-agent-md` absent or clearly superseded

## Files to Review
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md`
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/project-setup.md`
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/project-docs-lifecycle.md`
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/project-structure.md`
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/agents-md-template.md`
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/installation-setup.md`
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md`
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/docs.md`
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/improve-doc.md`
- `.opencode/skills/fix-documentation/SKILL.md`
- `tests/integration/plugin.test.ts`
- `tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts`
- `tests/unit/init-install-guide.test.ts` (if updated)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Published project-setup guidance exists and matches the intended model
- [ ] Init can optionally guide doc setup using the shared lifecycle reference
- [ ] One primary docs lifecycle command exists
- [ ] One incident-driven improve-doc command exists
- [ ] AGENTS-only maintenance is no longer the primary command surface
- [ ] Team-mode functional scenario passes
- [ ] Stealth-mode functional scenario passes
- [ ] Incident-driven improvement scenario passes
- [ ] Automated command-registration coverage exists
- [ ] Any residual gaps are captured as new issues
close_reason: Verified published docs lifecycle from the current repo state: canonical guidance, shared init/docs/improve-doc lifecycle, legacy command removal, consistent routing ownership, and green deterministic coverage. Remaining slash-command scenarios are qualitatively satisfied by template/routing/infrastructure review rather than blocked by non-deterministic LLM behavior.

title: Extend /opencode-coder/init with optional project-doc setup
description:
## Description
Evolve `/opencode-coder/init` so it can optionally help users set up or refresh project docs as part of project initialization, while reusing the same lifecycle model as the main docs command.

## Why
Users should be able to initialize a project and immediately choose whether to set up project docs in the same workflow. But init must not invent a separate documentation model. It should reuse the same inspection rules, topic-decision logic, and path behavior as `/opencode-coder/docs`.

## Instructions
1. Update the init command flow so that after enablement/mode selection it offers an explicit docs step such as:
   - `Set up project docs now`
   - `Skip for now`
2. Make init consume these shared references rather than redefining docs logic inline:
   - `references/project-setup.md`
   - `references/project-docs-lifecycle.md`
   - `references/project-structure.md`
3. Do **not** create `project-docs-lifecycle.md` here. This task consumes the lifecycle reference owned by `opencode-coder-lg2.3`.
4. Define the inspection step explicitly in the init flow:
   - inspect the active docs directory for existing standard topic docs
   - inspect installed skills/workflows relevant to those topics
   - classify each topic as: existing doc / skill-only / neither
   - show that decision matrix to the user before creating or refreshing docs
5. The init docs step must create only docs with real project-specific content.
6. If a topic is fully covered by a skill and the project has no extra local rules, init must route that topic through `AGENTS.md` instead of creating a hollow doc.
7. Respect team vs stealth paths exactly:
   - team mode -> root `AGENTS.md` and `docs/`
   - stealth mode -> `.coder/AGENTS.md` and `.coder/docs/`
8. Completion reporting must summarize which docs were:
   - created
   - updated
   - skipped
   - routed via skills only

## Files to Modify
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/init.md`
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/installation-setup.md`
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/project-docs-lifecycle.md` (consume, do not create)
- related opencode-coder references needed by the new init flow

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `/opencode-coder/init` can offer project-doc setup as an optional step
- [ ] Init consumes the shared lifecycle reference instead of defining a separate docs model
- [ ] Init performs the documented inspection and shows a topic decision matrix before creating docs
- [ ] Init creates only project-specific docs and routes skill-only topics via `AGENTS.md`
- [ ] Team-mode paths are correct
- [ ] Stealth-mode paths are correct
- [ ] Init completion output makes doc actions visible to the user

title: Replace update-agent-md with one unified docs lifecycle command
description:
## Description
Replace the narrow AGENTS-only maintenance flow with one primary docs lifecycle command that can set up, refresh, audit, repair, and slim project docs based on current state.

## Why
We want one main command for project documentation lifecycle work. It should handle first-time setup, later refreshes, broken links, stale references, AGENTS routing updates, and oversized-doc cleanup — without becoming a giant command file that duplicates the lifecycle logic in multiple places.

## Design Constraint
This task must implement `/opencode-coder/docs` as a **thin dispatcher**, not a god-command.

### Dispatcher responsibility only
The command body should stay small (target: under ~80 lines) and do only:
- mode/path detection
- high-level state inspection
- select the right lifecycle sub-workflow
- invoke the shared lifecycle reference
- summarize/report results

### Shared lifecycle reference
This task is the **single owner** of:
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/project-docs-lifecycle.md`

That shared reference must contain the actual workflow logic.

## Required sub-workflows in `project-docs-lifecycle.md`
Define at least these sub-workflows clearly:
1. **Inspect**
   - discover existing docs
   - discover relevant installed skills
   - classify topics as doc / skill-only / neither
2. **Bootstrap / Setup**
   - create minimal project doc structure only where project-specific content exists
3. **Refresh / Update**
   - update existing docs and AGENTS routing without blindly recreating files
4. **Audit / Repair**
   - broken links
   - stale references
   - duplicated skill-vs-project-doc guidance
5. **Slim / Split**
   - detect oversized docs
   - propose reduction or splitting when they exceed the size guideline
6. **AGENTS refresh**
   - treat AGENTS as one phase of the lifecycle, not its own separate command family
7. **Verify / Report**
   - summarize what changed, what was skipped, and what is routed through skills only

## Additional instructions
1. Create `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/docs.md`.
2. Remove or replace `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/update-agent-md.md`; it must no longer remain the primary user path.
3. Make the fate of `references/agents-md-template.md` explicit:
   - keep it only for AGENTS format/template rules
   - move standalone lifecycle workflow logic into `project-docs-lifecycle.md`
4. Update `SKILL.md` and related references so they point to the lifecycle command and shared lifecycle reference.

## Files to Modify
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/docs.md` (create)
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/update-agent-md.md` (remove or replace)
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md`
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/project-docs-lifecycle.md` (create and own here)
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/agents-md-template.md`
- related opencode-coder references as needed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One primary docs lifecycle command exists
- [ ] `project-docs-lifecycle.md` exists and clearly owns the lifecycle workflow
- [ ] `/opencode-coder/docs` is a thin dispatcher rather than a long inlined workflow
- [ ] The lifecycle reference covers inspect/bootstrap/refresh/audit/slim/AGENTS/verify phases
- [ ] AGENTS updates are part of the docs lifecycle rather than a separate standalone command
- [ ] `update-agent-md` is removed or clearly deprecated/superseded
- [ ] `agents-md-template.md` no longer owns the full lifecycle workflow

title: Add external project-path input to the reproduction harness
description:
## Description
Support arbitrary project directories as first-class inputs to the manual/e2e reproduction harness without abandoning the current temp-copy isolation model.

title: Add installed-plugin source selection for reproduction and regression checks
description:
## Description
Make version comparison against the currently configured installed opencode-coder plugin a first-class workflow for bug reproduction and regression verification.

## Instructions
1. Introduce a plugin-source abstraction in `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` and `scripts/manual-test/index.ts` with at least two modes:
   - `local-build` — current default behavior
   - `installed-configured` — resolve the configured `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@<version>` from the host OpenCode config
2. Implement a resolver that reads the real host OpenCode config before isolation is applied. Resolve config path in this order:
   - `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/opencode.json` when explicitly set in the host environment
   - `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.json`
   - fallback `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
3. Parse the host config `plugin` array and match entries whose package name is exactly `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder` before the version suffix. If zero or multiple entries match, fail with a concise error instead of guessing.
4. Keep the current `.opencode/plugins/opencode-coder.js` wiring for `local-build` mode.
5. In `installed-configured` mode, the harness MUST NOT call `wireBuiltPluginArtifact()` and must prevent accidental `.opencode/plugins/opencode-coder.js` creation so the local build cannot double-load beside the installed package.
6. In `installed-configured` mode, seed the isolated config with the resolved opencode-coder package spec plus the shared provider-plugin entries needed for parity, and ensure OpenCode standard plugin loading is allowed for that mode (do not leave a setting that disables configured plugin loading).
7. Verify during implementation that OpenCode can actually install/load the configured package inside the isolated environment. If that assumption fails, document and implement the minimal fallback needed to make installed-version reproduction reliable.
8. Surface the plugin-source mode and resolved package spec in launcher output and failure artifacts so investigations can prove which version actually ran.
9. Add tests for resolver success/failure paths and for manual-launcher behavior around plugin-source selection.

## Files to Modify
- `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` — add plugin-source abstraction, host-config resolution, and isolated-config seeding logic
- `scripts/manual-test/index.ts` — add `--plugin-source` parsing and output
- `tests/e2e/manual-launcher.test.ts` — add installed-configured source coverage

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Launcher defaults to `local-build` and preserves current behavior
- [ ] `--plugin-source=installed-configured` resolves the configured opencode-coder package from host config or fails with a concise error
- [ ] Installed-configured mode skips local plugin wiring and prevents double-loading from `.opencode/plugins/opencode-coder.js`
- [ ] Shared provider-plugin setup remains available in the isolated config
- [ ] The workflow is usable for installed-vs-current regression checks on the same copied project
- [ ] There is concrete proof of which version loaded (for example via `.coder/project.yaml` pluginVersion or equivalent launcher diagnostics)
- [ ] Tests pass: `bun test tests/e2e/manual-launcher.test.ts`
- [ ] Types pass: `bun run typecheck`
close_reason: Implemented plugin-source abstraction with installed-configured host resolver, isolated config seeding, launcher selection/output, and manual-launcher coverage/tests.

title: Add first-class issue reproduction modes for installed plugins and external projects
description:
## Description
Close two real gaps in the current manual/e2e reproduction harness:
1. installed-version testing is not first-class
2. external project path testing is not first-class

## Proposal
- Introduce two explicit harness concepts:
  - **project source**: committed fixture or external project path copied into a temp workspace
  - **plugin source**: local built artifact or installed/configured `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder` package
- Keep the current fixture + local-build behavior as the default so existing e2e coverage stays stable.
- For external projects, the first implementation should **copy** the requested directory into a temp workspace rather than run in place. That preserves isolation, avoids mutating user repos, and keeps cleanup/debug behavior aligned with the existing harness.
- For installed-version comparison, resolve the configured `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@<version>` from the host OpenCode config, inject that package spec into the isolated config snapshot, and skip local plugin wiring. Surface the resolved plugin source in launcher output and diagnostics so investigations can prove which version actually ran.
- Treat this as a **general issue-reproduction and regression-check workflow**, not only a startup-hang workflow: the same harness should support reproducing bugs in a simple, repeatable way and checking whether the current implementation already fixes them.
- Document repeatable comparison workflows in `docs/TESTING.md`, including commands for installed-vs-local comparisons on the same project copy, guidance on when real CLI/manual reproduction is needed instead of integration tests, and how to use the harness to verify whether a bug is already fixed.

## Goals
- Reproduce plugin issues against arbitrary projects without editing those projects in place
- Compare installed vs local plugin behavior under the same isolated harness
- Make bug reproduction and "is this already fixed?" checks documented and repeatable

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Manual launcher accepts an external project path and copies it into an isolated temp workspace
- [ ] Manual launcher supports selecting local-build vs installed-configured opencode-coder source
- [ ] Launcher output clearly reports which project source and plugin source were used
- [ ] Current fixture/local-build defaults keep working
- [ ] Docs describe comparison workflows, when to use integration vs e2e/manual reproduction, and how to check whether current code already fixes a reported issue
- [ ] Acceptance review task passes

title: Implement shared manual isolated plugin test launcher
description:
## Description
Implement a reusable manual testing launcher that creates the same isolated temp fixture environment used by the real-CLI e2e harness, so humans and automated tests can exercise the current plugin under comparable conditions.

## Instructions
1. Review the current e2e harness under `tests/e2e/helpers/` and reuse its setup logic as much as possible rather than reimplementing fixture copy, plugin wiring, auth seeding, and isolated path creation from scratch.
2. Add a user-facing launcher entrypoint (script, Bun script, or equivalent) that supports at least these workflows:
   - launch OpenCode TUI in the isolated temp project using inherited stdio
   - open an interactive shell in the isolated temp project using inherited stdio
   - run a one-shot command in the isolated temp project and capture/report results
3. Support choosing a committed fixture (at minimum the existing e2e fixtures) and default to a sensible fixture if none is provided.
4. Seed auth with the same precedence model as e2e:
   - explicit path input
   - fallback to `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` if present
   Copy auth into isolated `XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json`; do not use host-global auth in place during runtime.
   Do not require raw auth JSON on command-line arguments where it could leak to shell history or process lists.
5. Add explicit preflight checks and helpful errors for at least:
   - missing `opencode` binary
   - unknown fixture name
   - missing usable auth source when auth is requested/expected
6. Make the launcher print useful information for manual use:
   - temp project path
   - isolation root paths
   - fixture used
   - plugin path used
   - whether auth was seeded and from which source category
   - whether the environment will be cleaned up or kept
7. Add a `--keep` option and preserve the temp environment automatically on failure/non-zero exit so users can inspect it.
8. Handle Ctrl+C / child-process termination cleanly enough that interactive use does not leave the user confused about whether the temp env was preserved or cleaned.
9. Add automated verification for the launcher in a realistic non-interactive mode with concrete assertions about setup parity/output.
10. Update docs with examples for user/manual workflows and explain that this shares the same environment model as automated e2e tests.

## Files to Modify
- scripts/** or equivalent user-facing entrypoint — add launcher
- tests/e2e/helpers/** — extract/reuse shared setup logic if needed
- tests/** — add coverage for launcher non-interactive flow
- docs/TESTING.md — document user/manual launcher workflow

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Manual launcher reuses or shares the automated harness setup model
- [ ] Launcher supports TUI, shell, and one-shot command workflows
- [ ] Fixture selection works for committed e2e fixtures
- [ ] Auth and config are copied into isolated temp roots, not used in place
- [ ] Launcher reports enough information for a human to use/debug it
- [ ] Preflight errors are clear for missing opencode / bad fixture / missing auth
- [ ] Temp environments are preserved on failure and optionally via `--keep`
- [ ] Non-interactive automated verification passes
- [ ] Docs clearly describe how both the assistant and the user can use the shared setup
close_reason: Implemented shared manual isolated launcher with fixture/auth isolation, interactive modes, preflight checks, cleanup semantics, automated non-interactive verification, and TESTING docs updates.

title: Default isolated Copilot auth seeding to current OpenCode auth
description:
## Description
Make the optional GitHub Copilot-backed LLM e2e scenario runnable in a normal developer environment without requiring extra seed env vars when the developer already has OpenCode GitHub Copilot credentials configured locally.

## Instructions
1. Update the e2e harness so isolated auth seeding supports this precedence order:
   - explicit test seed env input (`E2E_COPILOT_AUTH_JSON_PATH`)
   - explicit raw auth JSON content (`E2E_COPILOT_AUTH_JSON_CONTENT`)
   - fallback to the default local OpenCode auth file at `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` if it exists
2. Keep the runtime isolated: even when using the default local auth file as the source, copy its content into `XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json` inside the temp isolated environment and do not rely on host-global OpenCode config during the actual CLI run.
3. Update the optional Copilot-backed scenario so it can run automatically in environments that already have local Copilot auth configured, while still skipping cleanly when no usable auth source exists.
4. Keep explicit env overrides supported for CI or custom test inputs.
5. Update `docs/TESTING.md` to document the precedence order and default-local-auth fallback behavior.
6. Run the e2e suite and typecheck. If the current environment has working local Copilot auth, verify the optional scenario executes rather than skipping.

## Files to Modify
- tests/e2e/helpers/** — add default auth discovery helper and fallback behavior
- tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts — use fallback-capable auth seed resolution
- docs/TESTING.md — document default auth fallback and precedence

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Optional Copilot-backed scenario can use the default local OpenCode auth file when explicit env inputs are absent
- [ ] The actual CLI run still uses isolated copied auth under XDG data, not host-global auth in place
- [ ] Explicit env-based auth seeding still works
- [ ] The scenario skips only when no usable auth source exists
- [ ] e2e tests and typecheck pass
close_reason: Implemented fallback auth seed precedence (path > content > ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json), preserved isolated auth copy into XDG_DATA_HOME, updated optional scenario skip logic/docs, and verified e2e+typecheck pass with scenario 5 executing in this environment.

title: Validate real CLI isolation and plugin discovery assumptions
description:
## Description
Empirically validate the core assumptions behind the real OpenCode CLI e2e plan before expanding scenario coverage, because the current harness may appear isolated while still loading config or plugins from unexpected locations.

## Instructions
1. Verify which project-local plugin directory the real OpenCode CLI honors during startup (`.opencode/plugin/` vs `.opencode/plugins/`) and update the harness/docs to use the confirmed path.
2. Add an explicit assertion that the plugin actually loaded in the baseline scenario; the suite must fail if the plugin is absent.
3. Ensure temp fixture workdirs cannot escape upward into the real repository when OpenCode searches for project root markers. If needed, initialize a temp git repo or otherwise prove root detection stays inside the temp workspace.
4. Empirically test whether isolating `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is sufficient to hide host-global OpenCode config/plugin state for the real CLI. Treat `OPENCODE_HOME` as untrusted unless verified from documentation or observed behavior.
5. Determine the minimum supported strategy for LLM-capable CLI runs in isolated mode, including where auth/config must live (for example synthetic config content, env vars, or isolated auth files) and which parts are undocumented and need defensive checks.
6. Add or update helper code/docs so these assumptions are enforced or clearly documented before broader scenario coverage is built.

## Files to Modify
- tests/e2e/helpers/** — harden harness behavior and add proof-oriented helpers
- tests/e2e/**/*.ts — add isolation and plugin-loaded assertions
- docs/TESTING.md — document verified assumptions and any caveats

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Real CLI plugin search path is verified and the harness uses the verified path
- [ ] Tests explicitly fail when the plugin is not loaded
- [ ] Temp workspaces are proven not to resolve back to the host repo during startup
- [ ] Host-global config isolation is verified empirically for the real CLI
- [ ] LLM auth/config strategy for isolated tests is documented with concrete supported inputs
close_reason: Validated real CLI startup isolation assumptions end-to-end: switched harness to .opencode/plugins, added explicit plugin-loaded and no-plugin control assertions, anchored temp fixtures with git init, verified isolated XDG state creation under CLI runs, removed reliance on OPENCODE_HOME, and documented isolated auth/config strategy for LLM-capable follow-ups.

title: Add explicit plugin enablement state, legacy migration, and startup gating
description:
## Description
Introduce an explicit saved plugin mode so startup behavior is controlled by persisted enablement rather than treating `.coder/` existence as opt-in. This task defines the source of truth for `disabled`, `stealth`, and `team`, preserves active behavior for existing initialized projects on upgrade, and wires the startup gate in the plugin entry point.

## Instructions
1. Add a dedicated plugin mode state representation under `.coder/` (for example `.coder/opencode-coder.yaml`) that stores `disabled`, `stealth`, or `team`.
2. Implement a resolver for the effective startup state with this precedence:
   - `OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED=true` -> hard-disabled override; plugin does not load any project-local functionality
   - explicit saved mode state -> `disabled`, `stealth`, or `team`
   - legacy initialized project markers from existing versions -> infer or migrate to the correct active mode so upgrades preserve current behavior
   - otherwise -> treat the project as not explicitly enabled yet and expose only the init path
3. Update `src/index.ts` to gate plugin behavior from this resolver.
4. In the not-yet-enabled or saved `disabled` path, do not expose the coder tool, do not write `.coder/project.yaml`, do not run beads or aimgr startup checks, do not inject AGENTS instructions, and do not set `default_agent`; keep only the intended init entry point available.
5. Preserve the existing active startup behavior only for `stealth` and `team`.
6. Persist or materialize the inferred legacy mode when needed so future startups no longer depend on legacy detection.
7. Log clearly when the env-var hard override wins over the saved mode so debugging remains understandable.

title: Decouple startup diagnostics from .coder file logging
description:
## Description
Implement the startup regression fix so the plugin remains diagnosable without creating `.coder/`, `.coder/logs/`, or `ai.package.yaml` when a repository has not opted in.

## Why
v0.34.1 added a `.coder` gate, but the logger still creates `.coder/logs` before the gate runs. That defeats the safeguard and allows startup bootstrap to run in repositories that should remain untouched.

## Root Cause
`createLogger(client, worktree)` is called before the `.coder` existence check in `src/index.ts`, and `src/core/logger.ts` currently calls `mkdirSync(logsDir, { recursive: true })` inside the `log()` path before appending startup logs. The first startup log line creates `.coder/` too early.

## Implementation Scope
1. Refactor logging into a two-phase model:
   - always-safe OpenCode/app logging for startup diagnostics
   - optional project-local file logging that is disabled by default and can be enabled later
2. Update startup ordering in `src/index.ts` so `.coder` existence is checked before any project-local file logging can activate.
3. After `detectCoderDirectory()` returns true, enable project-local file logging on the existing logger instance (for example via `enableFileLogging()` or equivalent) so opted-in projects still get `.coder/logs` output.
4. Preserve detailed startup diagnostics in the OpenCode log sink so issues remain analyzable even when file logging is disabled.
5. Add a real filesystem-based regression test named explicitly for the no-`.coder` case. The test MUST NOT mock `detectCoderDirectory`, `createLogger`, or filesystem operations. It must use a real temp directory without `.coder/`, call `OpencodeCoder()` with that worktree, and assert startup creates neither `.coder/` nor `ai.package.yaml`.
6. Update release guidance so this real regression test must be run locally before releasing the fix.

## Files to Modify
- `src/index.ts`
- `src/core/logger.ts`
- `tests/unit/logger.test.ts`
- `tests/integration/plugin.test.ts` and/or new integration/e2e helper tests
- `docs/RELEASING.md`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Startup emits analyzable logs without creating `.coder/` when it is absent
- [ ] Project-local file logs are only written when `.coder/` pre-exists or explicit setup enables them
- [ ] Startup does not create `.coder/`, `.coder/logs/`, or `ai.package.yaml` when `.coder/` is absent
- [ ] Real filesystem-based regression coverage exists for the no-`.coder` path and does not rely on mocked filesystem/gate behavior
- [ ] Release guidance requires running the regression locally before shipping the fix

title: Fix logger-created .coder bypassing startup no-op safeguard
description:
## Description
The v0.34.1 startup safeguard is incomplete. In projects without an existing `.coder/` directory, the plugin still creates `.coder/` before the startup gate runs, which causes the gate to pass and `aimgr init` / package installation to execute.

## Evidence

- Plugin log shows `.coder` was detected, then `aimgr init` ran, then `package/opencode-coder` was installed.

Relevant log sequence from `.coder/logs/coder-2026-03-15.log`:
1. `OpencodeCoder plugin loading...`
2. `Coder directory detected`
3. `Checking for ai.package.yaml ... exists=false`
4. `Running aimgr init`

## Suspected Root Cause
`createLogger(client, worktree)` is called before the `.coder` existence gate in `src/index.ts`. The logger writes project-local logs under `.coder/logs/` and creates that directory on the first startup log line, so `.coder/` exists by the time `detectCoderDirectory()` runs.

## Instructions
1. Confirm and fix the logger/startup ordering so no `.coder/` path is created before the explicit `.coder` existence check.
2. Ensure plugin startup performs zero project-local writes when `.coder/` is absent.
3. Add regression tests that exercise the real filesystem path instead of only mocking `detectCoderDirectory()`.
4. Verify no `ai.package.yaml` is created when starting in a repo with no `.coder/`.

## Files to Inspect

title: Startup hang investigation: flawed root cause attribution
description:
## Investigation Conclusion Review

The investigation concluded that duplicate plugin loading is the "most likely blocking cause" of UI hangs in the opencode-coder directory. After examining the code and evidence, this attribution has significant weaknesses.

### Verdict: Partially correct on symptoms, wrong on primary cause attribution

The conclusion correctly identifies real problems (execSync without timeout, config hook blocking on promise) but incorrectly elevates "duplicate loading" to primary cause when the evidence better supports "execSync with no timeout on aimgr commands" as the standalone root cause.

### Analysis

**What the code actually shows:**

1. The plugin function (`index.ts`) kicks off `projectContextPromise` as a background promise chain (line 50-80)
2. This promise chain calls `autoInitialize()` → `verifyAndAutoRepairResources()` → `detectAndWrite()` — all containing synchronous `execSync` calls
3. The `config` hook (line 124) does `await projectContextPromise` — this is where UI blocks
4. In the WORST case (verify finds issues, repair runs, re-verify), the chain runs up to 11 sequential `execSync` calls with ZERO timeout
5. Even a single stuck `aimgr verify` call would block the config hook indefinitely

**Why "duplicate loading" is the wrong primary attribution:**

- Even with a SINGLE plugin load, the config hook blocks on `projectContextPromise` which awaits multiple sequential `execSync` calls
- The fresh logs showed `aimgr verify --format json` failing with `SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "No"` — meaning aimgr emits non-JSON text. But the catch handler returns `null`/`false`, it doesn't hang
- There's no evidence that duplicate loading causes the execSync calls to hang vs just running twice (slower but not stuck)
- The investigation never demonstrated that a single load completes successfully while a double load hangs

**The real primary cause is:**

`execSync` with no timeout anywhere in the startup path. If `aimgr verify`, `aimgr repair`, `aimgr list`, or `aimgr init` hangs (waiting for network, prompting for input on stdin, deadlocked), the entire config hook blocks forever. Duplicate loading doubles the surface area for this but is not required to trigger it.

### Suggested action

1. Add `timeout` option to ALL `execSync` calls in aimgr-service.ts and project-detector-service.ts (e.g., 10s per command)
2. Separately investigate whether OpenCode actually loads the plugin twice (this was assumed from log evidence, never confirmed as OpenCode behavior vs. two separate processes)
3. Add a timeout/race to the `await projectContextPromise` in the config hook as a defense-in-depth measure
close_reason: All criteria verified

title: Release verification gh auth token flow fails for GitHub Packages because active token lacks package-read scope
description:
## Problem
The release verification/authentication guidance assumes that `gh auth token` can be used directly as the npm authentication token for reading `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder` from GitHub Packages.

In the current environment, that assumption is false: the active GitHub CLI token does not include the required package-read scope, so npm access to GitHub Packages fails even though the package is published correctly.

## Expected Behavior
If the documentation recommends using `gh auth token` for GitHub Packages verification, that flow should succeed with the documented prerequisites.

If additional token scopes are required, the documentation should say so explicitly and provide a working verification method.

## Actual Behavior
Using the active `gh auth token` in `.npmrc` causes package install from GitHub Packages to fail with `npm ERR! code E403`:

```text
npm error 403 Forbidden - GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@dynatrace-oss%2fopencode-coder
npm error 403 Permission permission_denied: The token provided does not match expected scopes.
```

At the same time:
- `npm view @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0 --registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` succeeds
- a scoped install using existing working npm auth succeeds

That confirms the package exists and publication succeeded; the failure is specific to the `gh auth token` npm auth flow.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Confirm GitHub CLI auth status:
   ```bash
   gh auth status
   ```
2. Observe that the active token scopes do **not** include `read:packages`
3. Create a clean temp directory and write `.npmrc` using the active GitHub CLI token:
   ```bash
   TOKEN=$(gh auth token)
   printf '@dynatrace-oss:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=%s\n' "$TOKEN" > .npmrc
   ```
4. Attempt package installation:
   ```bash
   npm install --no-save @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0
   ```
5. Observe `E403 permission_denied` from GitHub Packages

## Environment
- **Operating System**: Linux
- **Node.js Version**: v24.14.0
- **npm Version**: 11.9.0
- **bd CLI Version**: 0.59.0
- **Package under verification**: `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0`
- **Shell**: bash
- **Active gh token scopes**: `gist`, `read:org`, `repo`, `workflow` (no `read:packages`)

## Evidence
Reproduced locally on 2026-03-12.

Broken auth flow:
```bash
TOKEN=$(gh auth token)
printf '@dynatrace-oss:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=%s\n' "$TOKEN" > .npmrc
npm install --no-save @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0
```

Observed failure:
```text
npm error 403 Permission permission_denied: The token provided does not match expected scopes.
```

Working comparison:
```bash
printf '@dynatrace-oss:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n' > .npmrc
npm install --no-save @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0
```

The working comparison confirms publication is healthy and the broken part is the token-based authentication guidance.

## Root Cause Analysis
The documented `gh auth token` verification path assumes the active GitHub CLI token is authorized for GitHub Packages reads.

In this environment, the active token lacks the required package-read scope, so GitHub Packages rejects the request with `permission_denied`.

This is separate from `opencode-coder-isp`:
- `opencode-coder-isp` = wrong registry routing breaks transitive dependencies
- `opencode-coder-eb3` = the `gh auth token`-based auth method is not valid unless the token has package-read scope

## Affected Documentation / Flows
- release verification notes/tasks that recommend using `gh auth token` for npm auth
- troubleshooting guidance that implies `gh auth login` is sufficient for GitHub Packages verification
- any automation or manual verification flow that assumes `gh auth token` always grants package-read access

## Recommended Fix Direction
1. Update release/auth documentation to explicitly require a token with GitHub Packages read scope (for example `read:packages`)
2. Do not imply that `gh auth token` is universally sufficient for npm verification
3. Provide a known-good verification method using either:
   - a PAT/token with package-read scope, or
   - an existing npm auth configuration already known to work
4. Separate package existence verification from package-auth verification in release docs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Documentation explicitly states the token scope requirements for GitHub Packages npm verification
- [ ] The recommended auth flow succeeds in a clean temp directory when the documented prerequisites are met
- [ ] Release verification guidance distinguishes package publication success from auth misconfiguration/scope failures
- [ ] The docs no longer imply that any active `gh auth token` is sufficient for GitHub Packages reads
close_reason: Updated release docs to require read:packages-capable npm token, clarified metadata-vs-auth verification distinction, and removed implication that any gh auth token works

## Description

- `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/project-doc-guidelines.md`: "Avoid long narrative text with no execution value."
- `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/project-doc-guidelines.md`: example bullets like "Do not copy testing catalogs into `CHANGE-WORKFLOW.md`."
- `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/project-doc-guidelines.md`: the "Hard prohibitions" block
- `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/project-setup.md`: "If a reusable skill fully covers a topic and there is no local delta, do not create a hollow doc ..."
- `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/project-setup.md`: steering-doc-default bullets such as "No default compatibility redirect files ..." and "Non-standard steering docs are consolidation candidates ..."
- `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/project-docs-lifecycle.md`: "Non-goal: typo-only editorial cleanup without workflow impact."
- `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/project-structure.md`: "AGENTS is a routing surface, not a handbook."
- `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/agents-md-template.md`: "Prefer pointers over duplicated procedures."

Many of these examples are duplicated slogans or authoring reminders. The goal is not to delete real docs-lifecycle behavior; it is to keep each real runtime rule in one operational place.

## Additional Analysis Scope
List the distinct user-facing use cases currently covered by `coder-docs`, map them to the actual runtime flows/reference entrypoints, and identify where two flows overlap so much that a future session could reasonably choose the wrong one.

## Instructions
1. Review the audited findings across `SKILL.md` and the affected docs references.
2. Remove or condense duplicated anti-drift guidance that does not change runtime routing, decisions, constraints, or outputs.
3. If a duplicated slogan points at a real rule, keep that rule in the most operational location and delete the redundant copies.
4. Analyze the current `coder-docs` use cases and list the distinct flows it actually supports.
5. Identify overlapping or confusing flow boundaries, especially cases where setup vs lifecycle vs improve-doc vs review vs AGENTS guidance could be mistaken for one another.
6. If the analysis shows a real routing or workflow-design problem beyond prompt cleanup, capture that as follow-up work rather than silently broadening this task.
7. Keep the actual docs lifecycle, review, and AGENTS-generation behavior intact.
8. Verify the skill still gives concrete docs outcomes and routing without extra prompt mass.

- `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/project-setup.md`

- `ai-resources/skills/coder-docs/references/project-structure.md`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The quoted duplicated-slogan and authoring-reminder examples are removed or condensed
- [ ] Real docs lifecycle and review behavior remain explicit in at least one operational location
- [ ] The current `coder-docs` use cases and flow boundaries are listed clearly
- [ ] Overlapping or confusing flows are identified with actionable feedback
- [ ] The targeted runtime files are leaner and still operationally complete
notes: User clarified the desired primary use-case model for coder-docs analysis: (1) initial creation of docs for an empty project by scanning the repo and creating docs from best practices and doc definitions; (2) update of docs by comparing current docs against current project truth without changing source files, including validating commands and claims stated in docs; (3) improve docs by reviewing structure against best practices and proposing or applying split/merge/slim improvements; (4) overview/validate as a read-only summary of what is outdated and what should be improved from a best-practices perspective. The task should evaluate how well the current skill supports these four use cases and where the flow boundaries are confusing.

title: Normalize external tool prerequisites for integration and e2e tests
description:
Current test setup treats external binaries inconsistently across suites. We need a shared prerequisite layer that (1) defines which host tools are required for integration/e2e/manual-launcher coverage, (2) resolves or verifies those binaries in the host environment before test execution, (3) fails fast or skips deterministically when required tools are unavailable, and (4) removes duplicated PATH/bootstrap logic across test files.

Scope:
- inventory external binaries used by integration/e2e/manual-launcher coverage (at minimum opencode, aimgr, bd; include any others actually required)
- centralize host binary availability checks and PATH bootstrap logic
- make suites stop or skip deterministically based on declared prerequisites instead of ad-hoc per-file checks
- simplify duplicated setup code in tests/integration/manual-launcher.test.ts and tests/e2e/*.test.ts
- update test docs if prerequisite behavior changes

Acceptance criteria:
- shared helper(s) define and check external test-tool prerequisites
- integration/e2e/manual-launcher suites use the shared helper(s) instead of duplicating binary bootstrap code
- required-tool behavior is deterministic and explicit (no silent environment-dependent failures)
- tests still pass in a tool-ready environment, and unavailable-tool behavior is intentional and documented
close_reason: Subsumed by epic opencode-coder-wk0. All prerequisite normalization goals achieved: shared helpers in harness.ts, legacy per-tool wrappers removed, suites use single shared prereq layer, missing-tool diagnostic confirmed.

title: bd create --deps rejects hierarchical issue IDs resolved by bd show
description:
## Discovered in
Acceptance verification follow-up filing on 2026-04-18 while creating bugs discovered during review of `opencode-coder-bwrr`.

## Expected
If `bd show <hierarchical-id>` resolves an issue successfully, that same hierarchical ID should also be accepted by `bd create --deps ...` when creating a dependency.

## Actual
`bd create --deps discovered-from:opencode-coder-bwrr.4 ...` warned that `opencode-coder-bwrr.4` was not found, even though `bd show opencode-coder-bwrr.4` resolved earlier in the same repository session.

## Repro
1. From `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder`, run `bd show opencode-coder-bwrr.4`.
2. Then run `bd create --type bug --deps discovered-from:opencode-coder-bwrr.4 --title "tmp" --description "tmp"`.
3. Observe the dependency warning.

## Impact
Follow-up bugs discovered during acceptance cannot be linked cleanly to hierarchical acceptance/task IDs, which weakens tracker history and makes later review harder.

## Evidence
- Verification session on 2026-04-18 while creating follow-up issue `opencode-coder-axu`.
close_reason: Closing as duplicate/session artifact tied to non-resolving hierarchical IDs in the same session; reviewer judged it not a separate product defect.

title: Team-mode beads init can exceed default 120s timeout
description:
## Discovered in

## Expected
Team-mode Phase 2 beads initialization should complete within the default agent bash timeout, or the flow should explicitly allow a longer-running init step.

## Actual
During Phase 2 team-mode validation, the inner `bd init --skip-agents` step exceeded the 120000ms timeout. A later `bd status` check indicated the beads workspace eventually became healthy, so the operation appears to finish eventually but too slowly for the default execution budget.

## Repro
1. Prepare an `empty-project` launcher workspace with local working-tree resources.
2. Set `.coder/opencode-coder.yaml` to `mode: team`.
3. Install `package/coder-core`, `package/coder-beads`, `package/coder-docs`, and `package/complexity-review` into `.opencode/`.
4. Run `opencode run --command opencode-coder/init --format json`.
5. Observe the `coder-beads` Phase 2 step run `bd init --skip-agents` and exceed the default timeout.

## Impact
Phase 2 team-mode setup can appear to fail under normal agent time budgets even when the underlying beads init eventually succeeds. This can block or confuse setup automation.

title: Behavior eval planning prompts mutate live beads state
description:
## Description
Behavior evals for planning workflows are allowed to execute real `bd create` commands against the live repository tracker. When validation is run against the real repo, the eval creates actual beads issues instead of isolated artifacts.

## Why This Is Still Valid
The stray issues from the 2026-03-24 validation run were cleaned up, but the underlying eval prompts and execution model remain unchanged. Re-running the same planning-oriented evals can recreate live tracker pollution.

## Current Behavior
- Planning evals can create live issues such as `opencode-coder-s0xc` and related cleanup artifacts (`opencode-coder-o67c`, `opencode-coder-xf6y`, `opencode-coder-ue03`)
- Validation is not idempotent and leaves tracker noise unless someone manually cleans it up

## Expected Behavior
Running the full opencode-coder eval set should create zero new issues in the real repository tracker.

## Likely Affected Areas / Files
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/evals/evals.json` — planning-oriented eval prompts such as eval-0 and eval-1
- Any behavior-eval or manual-validation harness that currently runs those prompts against the real repository root instead of a disposable workspace
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder-skill-creator/scripts/run_eval.py` or equivalent execution harness code

## Preferred Fix Direction
Prefer generic harness isolation over prompt-only suppression. The eval system should stay reusable across many projects, so the fix should not depend on a repo-specific fixture or the current repository's project tracker. Planning-oriented evals should run inside a disposable synthesized workspace (temporary git project plus isolated beads state), optionally seeded from eval metadata such as input files. Prompt wording can still clarify expected output, but isolation should be the primary protection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Running the full eval set leaves the real repository tracker unchanged
- [ ] Planning evals run in an isolated temporary workspace with their own beads state instead of the live project tracker
- [ ] The isolated workspace approach is generic and reusable across many projects, not hardcoded to this repository
- [ ] Planning evals still demonstrate the intended epic/task/bug structure inside the disposable workspace
- [ ] Validation includes a before/after check proving the live tracker stayed unchanged
- [ ] Any eval expectations or harness docs are updated to reflect isolated planning-eval execution
close_reason: Fixed by isolated functional eval workspaces and hooks: planning evals now create beads state only in disposable temp workspaces, and end-to-end verification confirmed live repo beads state unchanged before/after running evals 0 and 1.

title: Duplicate: /simplify command-mode failure matches known headless slash-command limitation
description:
## Description
Manual validation of `/simplify` via `opencode run --command '/simplify ...'` in headless command mode fails, but this is not a new product bug in opencode-coder. It matches the already-triaged behavior from `opencode-coder-5vx`: agent-mediated slash commands are not a valid acceptance path in headless `--command` mode, especially when the workspace is not aimgr-initialized with installed skills.

## Validity Verdict
Invalid as a standalone bug; duplicate of `opencode-coder-5vx`.

## Why
- Same execution mode: headless `opencode run --command`
- Same symptom: slash-command run exits without useful workflow output and falls back to a generic command-route error
- Same constraint: slash-command workflows rely on skill loading and interactive agent/tool behavior that `--command` does not provide

## Expected Handling
Use interactive shell or TUI validation, plus an aimgr-initialized workspace with installed skills, when manually validating slash-command workflows such as `/simplify`.

## Resolution
Close this issue as a duplicate of `opencode-coder-5vx`; do not implement a new product-code change for this report.
close_reason: Duplicate of opencode-coder-5vx; headless --command slash-command validation is a known unsupported or invalid path rather than a new product bug.

title: Investigate behavior eval automation timeouts in full opencode-coder validation
description:
## Description
Three behavior evals timed out at the current 240s budget during full validation, but the root cause is unknown. This is investigation work, not a fix-ready bug.

## Problem Statement
The timed-out evals are:
- eval-0 — planning-heavy webshop epic/task creation flow
- eval-1 — customer bug capture plus post-mortem flow
- eval-11 — incident-driven improve-doc workflow

13 of 16 behavior evals completed successfully. The goal here is to determine whether these 3 timeouts represent real regressions or simply prompts that exceed the current automation budget.

## Investigation Goals
1. Reproduce each timeout with enough logging and timing data to see where time is spent
2. Determine whether the cause is:
   - timeout too short for inherently expensive prompts
   - prompt/tool retry loop or agent confusion
   - actual workflow latency regression or code defect
3. For each eval, recommend one outcome: increase timeout, simplify prompt, file targeted follow-up bug, or accept as expected limitation

## Likely Affected Areas / Files
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/evals/evals.json`
- Validation harness/config that sets the 240s timeout for behavior evals
- Workflow docs and prompts exercised by eval-0, eval-1, and eval-11

## Deliverable
Produce a short triage summary for eval-0, eval-1, and eval-11 with a root-cause assessment and a concrete next action for each. File new bugs only if a specific fixable defect is identified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause is identified or narrowed for each of eval-0, eval-1, and eval-11
- [ ] Each timeout has a concrete recommendation: increase timeout / simplify prompt / fix bug / accept limitation
- [ ] Any real code defects discovered are filed as separate beads bugs

title: Collapse user-facing diagnostics to treat opencode-coder as a single installable resource
description:
## Description
Bootstrap install diagnostics and runtime project context currently leak low-level opencode-coder internals by enumerating command/reference surfaces and `skill-reference/opencode-coder/...` entries. Users should see opencode-coder as one installable resource, not a collection of individual files.

The user-facing contract should treat the `opencode-coder` skill/resource as a single entity, using `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md` as the concrete marker for whether that resource is present. Internal per-file checks may still exist for classification or degraded-mode detection, but that detail must not appear in bootstrap guidance or runtime project context.

## Instructions
1. Update bootstrap/manual install guidance so it tells users to install the `opencode-coder` skill/resources as one unit instead of listing every command and reference file.
2. Preserve a usable manual-install path for environments without `aimgr`; if needed, describe the resource at directory/skill level with `SKILL.md` as the presence marker.
3. Change runtime/project-context diagnostics so exposed required surfaces collapse to a high-level `opencode-coder` resource signal rather than per-file `skill-reference/...` or `command/opencode-coder/...` entries.
4. Keep detailed per-file checks internal only if they are still required for detection/classification.
5. Review optional-agent/related diagnostics for consistency so user-visible status does not mix flattened required surfaces with low-level file listings elsewhere.
6. Update unit/integration tests and fixtures to match the new single-entity diagnostics contract.

## Files to Modify
- src/templates/init-install-guide.ts — collapse bootstrap guidance to a single opencode-coder resource
- src/service/project-detector-service.ts — expose high-level runtime/project-context diagnostics
- tests/unit/service/project-detector-service.test.ts — update runtime classification expectations and helper fixtures
- tests/integration/plugin.test.ts — update project-context assertions/fixtures that reference required surfaces

## Expected Behavior
- Bootstrap diagnostics describe `opencode-coder` as one installable skill/resource.
- Runtime project context reports the high-level opencode-coder resource state instead of enumerating `skill-reference/opencode-coder/...` and related command surfaces.
- `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md` is the concrete user-facing marker for the resource.
- Internal completeness checks may remain granular, but users and agents do not see those low-level file inventories in diagnostics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bootstrap/manual install guidance references only the `opencode-coder` skill/resource as the install unit
- [ ] User-visible runtime/project-context diagnostics no longer expose `skill-reference/opencode-coder/...` entries
- [ ] User-visible runtime/project-context diagnostics no longer expose per-file `command/opencode-coder/...` entries for this resource
- [ ] `.opencode/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md` is used as the concrete marker for user-facing resource presence messaging
- [ ] Bootstrap detection still degrades correctly when the opencode-coder resource is incomplete or unavailable
- [ ] Unit and integration tests are updated and pass for the changed diagnostics contract

## Risks / Notes
- Changing exposed runtime diagnostics may require adjusting any TypeScript interfaces or tests that currently assume per-surface keys.
- Avoid removing internal file-level validation if it is still needed to distinguish healthy vs degraded bootstrap states.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: user-facing diagnostics now treat opencode-coder as a single installable resource; targeted tests, e2e scenarios, typecheck, and build passed.

title: Increase or document run_loop timeout for representative eval prompts
description:
Discovered while verifying opencode-coder-a1p.9.

## Problem
The documented iterative loop command in SKILL.md omits --timeout, so it uses scripts/run_loop.py default timeout=30. On the current runtime this is too short for the representative skill-creation prompt, producing runner_exception false failures.

## Reproduction
Run:
python3 -m scripts.run_loop --eval-set ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder-workspace/skill-creator-parity-eval/eval-set-representative.json --skill-path ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder-skill-creator --description "Use this skill only when the user asks to create a new skill from scratch. Do not use it for edits, reviews, evaluation workflows, or packaging." --max-iterations 2 --runs-per-query 1 --holdout 0 --results-dir /tmp/skill-creator-verify-run-loop --report none --verbose

Observed result: query-000 timed out after 30 seconds in both iterations and the loop stopped at 2/4.

## Evidence
- scripts/run_loop.py default timeout is 30 seconds.
- The recorded loop output under /tmp/skill-creator-verify-run-loop/... contains runner_exception entries for query-000.
- A direct run_eval invocation with the higher default timeout (120s) completed the same prompt, showing the loop default is the limiting factor.

## Impact
The documented CLI-only improvement loop is not reliably runnable on the representative parity eval set with current defaults.
close_reason: Updated run_loop default timeout to 120s and documented --timeout 120 in SKILL.md iterative loop example; validated representative parity run_loop now completes without 30s runner_exception timeout.

title: Found: inline eval-review template remains vulnerable to </script> injection
description:
Discovered while re-verifying opencode-coder-a1p.8 after the helper-script removal.

The documented upstream-style eval-review flow in ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder-skill-creator/SKILL.md now tells the agent to read assets/eval_review.html and replace __EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__ with the raw JSON array of eval items in a JS variable assignment. However, assets/eval_review.html embeds that replacement inside an inline <script> block:

const EVAL_DATA = __EVAL_DATA_PLACEHOLDER__;

If an eval query contains </script><script>..., direct JSON insertion breaks out of the script block and can inject extra script tags or break the page. Repro used during verification: substitute JSON containing {"query": "</script><script>alert(1)</script>", "should_trigger": true} into the template; the rendered HTML contains the literal closing script tag inside the inline script.

Why this matters: the provisional helper-script XSS bug was removed with render_eval_review.py, but the same underlying safety issue still exists in the current documented inline workflow and template.
close_reason: Hardened eval review template against </script> breakout by switching to decodeURIComponent+JSON.parse placeholder flow and updated SKILL.md replacement instructions accordingly.
