title: Manual launcher shell mode triggers zsh first-run prompt in isolated HOME
description:
## Description
When the manual launcher runs in shell mode and inherits SHELL=/bin/zsh, the isolated HOME used by the launcher has no zsh startup files, so zsh opens with the interactive zsh-newuser-install screen instead of a clean shell prompt.

## Reproduction
1. In this repo, run:
   SHELL=/bin/zsh bun run test:manual -- --mode=shell --fixture=cli-smoke-project
2. Observe the shell session after launcher setup.

## Expected
Shell mode should open directly into the requested isolated shell session without unexpected first-run setup UI.

## Actual
zsh shows the zsh-newuser-install wizard before the shell prompt. This adds unexpected interaction and can interfere with the intended manual-launcher shell UX.

## Evidence
Observed during acceptance review of opencode-coder-g3l on 2026-03-23. The launcher printed the normal setup summary, then zsh displayed the first-run configuration screen because HOME was isolated.
close_reason: Fixed manual launcher shell mode to seed isolated zsh startup file and prevent zsh-newuser-install prompt under isolated HOME.

title: Ignore and clean up e2e failure artifacts
description:
## Description
The e2e harness writes failure diagnostics under `tests/e2e/.artifacts/`, but that directory is currently not gitignored and some generated artifact files are already tracked in git. We need a sane, test-maintainer-friendly policy for where these artifacts live, how they are inspected, and how stale copies are cleaned up.

The current location is probably reasonable because it is test-local and already documented, but the workflow is incomplete unless generated artifacts are ignored, currently tracked artifact files are removed from the index, and there is a repeatable cleanup path.

Verification review concluded that the overall plan is sound, but it needs explicit handling for tracked-file migration and stale per-scenario data.

## Instructions
1. Keep `tests/e2e/.artifacts/` as the diagnostics location unless implementation work reveals a concrete reason it should move.
2. Add git ignore coverage for generated e2e artifacts so new failure logs do not show up as untracked files.
3. Remove any currently tracked files under `tests/e2e/.artifacts/` from the git index while preserving the intended local/generated workflow.
4. Add an explicit cleanup path for e2e artifacts.
   - Prefer a package script such as `clean:e2e-artifacts`.
   - Do not automatically delete all historical failure evidence on every default `test:e2e` run unless there is a strong reason; if you want a fresh-run mode, prefer making it explicit.
5. Review the harness write path and ensure repeated failures for the same scenario cannot leave stale extra files in that scenario folder.
6. Update testing documentation so contributors know:
   - what the directory is for
   - that it is intentionally untracked
   - how to clear it
   - whether artifacts persist across runs until manually cleaned
7. Verify the chosen workflow works in practice by exercising both artifact generation and cleanup.

## Files to Modify
- `.gitignore` — ignore `tests/e2e/.artifacts/`
- `package.json` — add cleanup script and optional fresh-run entrypoint only if justified
- `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` — clean stale per-scenario artifacts if needed
- `docs/TESTING.md` — document artifact purpose, retention, and cleanup workflow
- tracked files under `tests/e2e/.artifacts/` — remove from version control if they are generated outputs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New generated files under `tests/e2e/.artifacts/` are ignored by git
- [ ] Previously tracked generated artifact files under `tests/e2e/.artifacts/` are removed from the git index
- [ ] There is a documented, repeatable cleanup path for e2e artifacts
- [ ] Re-running the same scenario cannot leave stale extra files in that scenario folder
- [ ] Contributors can tell from `docs/TESTING.md` what the folder is for, whether it persists, and how to clear it
- [ ] Practical verification proves the workflow works:
  - generate an artifact and confirm it is ignored by git
  - confirm `git status --short -- tests/e2e/.artifacts` is clean for generated files
  - exercise the cleanup command and confirm artifacts are removed
close_reason: Implemented and verified e2e artifact workflow: artifacts ignored, previously tracked files removed from index, clean:e2e-artifacts works, and per-scenario rewrite clears stale files.

title: E2E scenarios 1 and 3 unconditionally assert docs lifecycle commands but require aimgr on PATH
description:
## Description
E2E scenarios 1 and 3 currently call docs-lifecycle command assertions unconditionally. That expectation only holds when `aimgr` is available on `PATH` and resource verification can mark the project healthy.

In aimgr-absent environments, the product behavior is currently correct: runtime resource verification reports unhealthy/unavailable state, docs lifecycle commands stay suppressed, and the real defect is that the tests still expect those commands to be present.

## Root Cause
- `AimgrService.isAimgrAvailable()` returns false when `aimgr` is not installed or not on `PATH`
- resource verification cannot mark the project healthy
- `projectContext.aimgr.resourcesHealthy` stays false
- runtime correctly exposes only the non-docs command surface
- scenarios 1 and 3 still assert docs lifecycle commands unconditionally

## Instructions
1. Update e2e coverage so scenarios 1 and 3 explicitly account for aimgr availability instead of always expecting docs lifecycle commands.
2. Preserve validation of active startup and plugin load even when aimgr is unavailable.
3. When aimgr is available, continue asserting docs lifecycle command exposure.
4. Update contributor/testing docs only if the conditional prerequisite needs to be called out explicitly.
5. Re-run targeted integration and e2e coverage for the affected scenarios.

## Files to Modify
- `tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts` — make scenario 1 and 3 command assertions conditional on aimgr availability
- `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` — add or expose an aimgr availability helper if needed
- `docs/TESTING.md` — document the aimgr prerequisite if command expectations become conditional

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Scenario 1 passes whether aimgr is present or absent
- [ ] Scenario 3 passes whether aimgr is present or absent
- [ ] Tests still assert docs lifecycle command exposure when aimgr is available
- [ ] Tests still verify active startup/plugin load when aimgr is unavailable
- [ ] Documentation matches the implemented prerequisite behavior
close_reason: E2E assertions now match aimgr-gated runtime behavior; targeted e2e and integration coverage pass.

title: Diagnostics bundle README reports readme artifact as missing
description:
## Description

## Why This Matters
The bundle is intended to be self-describing for humans and agents. A contradictory artifact summary inside the bundle can mislead triage and reduces confidence in the exported evidence.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `bun run diagnostics:collect` against any project root.
2. Open the generated `README.md` and inspect the `readme` row in the collected artifacts table.
3. Compare it with `manifest.json` for the same bundle.

## Actual Behavior
- `manifest.json` reports `artifacts.readme.status = "included"`.
- `README.md` shows the `readme` row as `missing`.

## Expected Behavior
- `README.md` should report the `readme` artifact as `included`.
- The README artifact table should stay consistent with `manifest.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Generated `README.md` reports the `readme` artifact as `included`
- [ ] `README.md` and `manifest.json` agree on artifact status for `readme`
- [ ] Deterministic coverage catches this regression
close_reason: Resolved diagnostics README/manifest inconsistency for readme artifact by updating write order and adding deterministic regression test.

title: Project-path launcher copies local .opencode and inherits broken symlink noise
description:
## Description
Discovered while verifying `opencode-coder-lg2.6`.

## Precise problem
This is primarily a **harness copy-scope bug**, not a repository-validity bug.

The manual launcher `--project-path` mode currently copies the source repository's local `.opencode/` directory into the isolated workspace. In this repository, `.opencode/` is local-only and may contain symlinks to external development resources. If those links are stale, the copied workspace inherits broken symlinks and OpenCode emits `failed to load command` ENOENT noise during startup.

## Root cause
`tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` excludes:
- `.git`
- `.beads`
- `.coder`

but it does **not** exclude `.opencode`.

That means isolated project-path runs inherit local developer-only `.opencode/commands` state even though the harness already rewires `.opencode/plugins/` intentionally for the plugin under test.

## Why this matters
This pollutes manual acceptance evidence with unrelated startup errors and makes the isolated workspace depend on local developer state.

## Correct scope
The right fix is to treat `.opencode/` like other local runtime/dev-only state for project-path copies.
This is about making the harness copy deterministic.

A follow-up repository-validation test is reasonable if we want to assert the tracked repo itself contains no broken committed links, but that is separate from this harness bug.

## Recommended fix direction
- exclude `.opencode/` from project-path copies in the harness
- add regression coverage that project-path copies do not inherit `.opencode/commands` noise
- optionally create a separate follow-up if we want a repo-validity check for committed resources

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Manual launcher project-path copies do not include source `.opencode/` runtime/dev-local state
- [ ] Startup no longer emits `failed to load command` ENOENT noise from copied broken `.opencode` links
- [ ] Regression coverage proves `.opencode` is excluded from project-path copies
close_reason: Excluded .opencode from project-path workspace copies in harness and added regression assertions in manual-launcher test to verify copied workspaces do not inherit .opencode command files/symlinks.

## Description

title: Add an incident-driven improve-doc command
description:
## Description
Add a second command for targeted documentation improvement when something went wrong because local guidance was missing, unclear, outdated, or routed incorrectly.

## Why
`/opencode-coder/docs` is the main lifecycle command. But we also want a focused command for cases like:
- "we forgot to run validate-before-release.sh"
- "the docs didn't explain the right release step"
- "AGENTS routed to the wrong place"

This command should learn from the failure and propose changes that prevent recurrence.

## Command model
Keep this as a separate command:
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/improve-doc.md`

It should still reuse the shared lifecycle reference rather than duplicating lifecycle logic.

## Instructions
1. Create `/opencode-coder/improve-doc` as a thin dispatcher that uses the incident-improvement section of `project-docs-lifecycle.md`.
2. Define the input contract explicitly:
   - optional free-text argument describing what went wrong
   - optional issue/reference identifier to pull context from a tracked bug/task
   - if no useful input is provided, prompt the user for failure context
3. Support examples such as:
   - `/opencode-coder/improve-doc "forgot to run validate-before-release.sh"`
   - `/opencode-coder/improve-doc --issue <id>` or equivalent issue-reference pattern
4. The workflow must identify whether the missing or weak guidance belongs in:
   - a project doc
   - AGENTS routing
   - the opencode-coder skill/reference
   - or some combination
5. The workflow must analyze why the current docs/routing did not prevent the issue.
6. The workflow must propose updates aimed at preventing recurrence.
7. This command is **not** for generic typo/grammar cleanup.

## Files to Modify
- `ai-resources/commands/opencode-coder/improve-doc.md` (create)
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/SKILL.md`
- `ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/references/project-docs-lifecycle.md`
- related opencode-coder references as needed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A targeted improve-doc command exists
- [ ] The command has an explicit input contract (text, issue/reference, or prompt fallback)
- [ ] The command can map a failure/omission to the right doc, routing, or skill gap
- [ ] The command focuses on recurrence prevention, not generic editorial cleanup
- [ ] The lifecycle reference explains how incident-driven improvement reuses the shared docs model
close_reason: Implemented /opencode-coder/improve-doc as a thin dispatcher with explicit incident input contract, shared lifecycle incident-improvement section, and discoverability updates.

title: Audit: opencode-coder skill — validation findings
description:
## Description
Full validation audit of the opencode-coder skill (ai-resources/skills/opencode-coder/).

Evaluated: trigger description quality, internal consistency, correctness/actionability of workflows, structure, missing/stale/contradictory guidance, and bundled resource usage.

## Scope
- SKILL.md (hub)
- 10 reference docs in references/
- 1 script in scripts/
- 1 asset in assets/

## Summary
The skill is well-structured as a lazy-load reference hub with 10 focused reference docs. Most workflows are actionable and internally consistent. However, there are several stale references to beads internals that no longer exist, a non-existent `bd stats` command reference, ambiguous script paths in bug-reporting.md, and the trigger description is overloaded. See comments for individual findings.

title: Docs still describe bd init as plugin setup after explicit enablement redesign
description:
Acceptance review for opencode-coder-0xg.6 found documentation that still presents manual beads initialization as a plugin setup/enablement path, which conflicts with the redesigned model where /opencode-coder/init is the sole documented setup entry point.

Findings:
- README.md says stealth/team mode can be enabled with bd init --stealth / bd init
- docs/user-guide/getting-started.md has an 'Optional manual setup' section that tells users to skip /opencode-coder/init and run bd init directly

Current implementation requires explicit saved mode state (.coder/opencode-coder.yaml) for active startup, so these docs do not match implemented behavior.

Expected:
- User-facing docs describe /opencode-coder/init as the setup entry point for enablement/mode selection
- Any manual beads instructions are clearly scoped as beads-only and not described as plugin activation
close_reason: Completed

title: Update docs for explicit plugin enablement, upgrade preservation, and hard-disable override
description:
## Description
Refresh user and developer documentation so the new explicit enablement model is clear. The docs need to explain that startup no longer creates project-local opencode-coder files before explicit enablement, that saved `disabled` mode keeps the plugin inactive until re-enabled, that existing initialized projects are preserved on upgrade, and that `OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED` is a separate hard override.

## Instructions
1. Update user-facing setup docs to describe the saved `disabled`, `stealth`, and `team` model.
2. Explain that fresh projects do not activate or create `.coder/` files until explicit init.
3. Document how existing initialized projects are preserved on upgrade.
4. Document saved `disabled` semantics clearly and explain how to re-enable via init.
5. Update command docs and getting-started material so `/opencode-coder/init` is the only setup command discussed.
6. Clearly distinguish saved `disabled` mode from `OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED`.

## Files to Modify
- `docs/user-guide/project-setup.md`
- `docs/user-guide/getting-started.md`
- `docs/user-guide/README.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] User docs explain saved `disabled`, `stealth`, and `team`
- [ ] Docs state that fresh startup does not create `.coder/` files before explicit enablement
- [ ] Docs describe how existing initialized projects continue to work after upgrade
- [ ] Docs describe `/opencode-coder/init` as the only setup entry point
- [ ] Docs distinguish saved `disabled` mode from `OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED`
- [ ] Changelog captures the activation model change
close_reason: Completed

title: Unnecessary dynamic imports of built-in modules in coder-tool.ts switch cases
description:
## Unnecessary dynamic imports: `await import('node:fs')` and `await import('node:path')` in tool switch cases

**File path**: `src/tool/coder-tool.ts` (lines 99-100, 137-139)

**What**: The `beads` and `logs` switch cases use dynamic `await import('node:fs')` and `await import('node:path')` to get `fs` and `path`. But:
1. `node:path` is already statically imported at line 3 (`import { isAbsolute, join } from 'node:path'`)
2. `node:fs` is a built-in module that's loaded at process startup — there's nothing to lazy-load

Dynamic imports of built-in Node modules incur a microtask round-trip for zero benefit. These aren't third-party modules that could fail to load or would save memory by lazy-loading.

**Why it matters**:
- Inconsistency: `path.join` from dynamic import on line 102 vs `join` from static import on line 76. Same module, two import styles in the same file.
- Unnecessary async: Each `await import` yields the event loop for no reason. For a tool that agents call frequently, this is avoidable overhead.
- Confusing signal: Dynamic imports usually mean 'this might not be available' or 'lazy-load heavy dependency'. Neither applies to `node:fs` and `node:path`.

**Suggested action**: Replace the dynamic imports with static imports at the top of the file:

```typescript
import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { isAbsolute, join } from 'node:path';
import { platform, homedir } from 'node:os';
```

Then use these directly in the switch cases.

**Risk**: None — built-in modules are always available, static import is strictly simpler.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Duplicate of opencode-coder-gzl — same finding (dynamic imports of builtins in coder-tool.ts)

title: coder-tool plugin sub-command bypasses isPluginDisabled — inconsistent env var parsing
description:
## Behavioral inconsistency: disabled-state check in coder-tool.ts vs config/env.ts

**File paths**:
- `src/tool/coder-tool.ts:89` — `process.env["OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED"] === "true"` (strict string match)
- `src/config/env.ts:20-32` — `parseBoolean()` (case-insensitive, trims whitespace)
- `src/index.ts:21` — uses `isPluginDisabled()` (the canonical check)

**Description**: The `plugin` sub-command in `coder-tool.ts` (line 89) reports the plugin's disabled status by checking `process.env["OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED"] === "true"`. But the *actual* disabled check in `src/index.ts` delegates to `isPluginDisabled()` which uses `parseBoolean()` — that accepts `"TRUE"`, `"True"`, `"  true  "`, etc.

This means `OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED=TRUE` will actually disable the plugin, but `coder("plugin")` will report `Status: ACTIVE`. The tool lies about its own state.

Same issue for the debug check: logger.ts uses `!!process.env['OPENCODE_CODER_DEBUG']` (any truthy value) while coder-tool.ts uses `=== "1"` (only the string "1").

**Why it matters**: When a user sets `OPENCODE_CODER_DISABLED=True` and the plugin is indeed disabled but the tool reports it as ACTIVE, that's a debugging trap. Debug mode has a similar mismatch.

**Suggested action**: Import and use `isPluginDisabled()` from `../config` instead of raw env-var access. For debug, either export an `isDebugEnabled()` helper from `config/env.ts` or use the same `parseBoolean` logic.

**Risk**: Very low — this is a display-only fix, no behavioral change to actual plugin loading.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

title: detectAimgrInstalled runs command -v aimgr twice during detectAndWrite
description:
## Double shell-out: `command -v aimgr` executed twice when resourcesHealthyOverride is not provided

**File path**: `src/service/project-detector-service.ts` (lines 435, 301, 438-443)

**What**: In `detectAndWrite`, line 435 calls `this.detectAimgrInstalled()` which runs `execSync('command -v aimgr')`. The result is stored in `aimgrInstalled`. Then on line 442, when `aimgrInstalled` is true and no override is provided, `this.detectResourcesHealthy()` is called — which **also** calls `this.detectAimgrInstalled()` on its first line (line 301), running `command -v aimgr` a second time.

```
detectAndWrite:
  line 435: detectAimgrInstalled() → execSync('command -v aimgr')  ← 1st call
  line 442: detectResourcesHealthy()
    line 301: detectAimgrInstalled() → execSync('command -v aimgr')  ← 2nd call (redundant)
    line 307: execSync('aimgr verify ...')
```

**Why it matters**: Each `execSync('command -v aimgr')` spawns a shell process and blocks the event loop. This is ~5-15ms of waste on each startup. The guard inside `detectResourcesHealthy` exists so it's safe to call standalone, but `detectAndWrite` already checks the precondition — it only reaches `detectResourcesHealthy` when `aimgrInstalled` is true.

**Suggested action**: Either:
- A) Pass `aimgrInstalled` into `detectResourcesHealthy` to skip its internal check, or
- B) Split `detectResourcesHealthy` into a guarded public version and an unguarded private `_verifyResourcesHealthy` that `detectAndWrite` calls directly when it already knows aimgr is installed.

Option A is simpler and keeps the API intact.

**Risk**: Very low — purely eliminating a redundant subprocess spawn.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Removed redundant aimgr availability shell-out in detectAndWrite and added regression coverage

title: mkdirSync called on every file log write — unnecessary syscall overhead
description:
## Redundant syscall: mkdirSync on every log line

**File path**: `src/core/logger.ts` (lines 30-33)

**What**: `writeFileLog` calls `mkdirSync(logsDir, { recursive: true })` before every `appendFileSync` call. After file logging is enabled (line 40), every single log line triggers a `mkdirSync` syscall to check/create a directory that already exists.

```typescript
const writeFileLog = (entry: BufferedFileLogEntry) => {
  mkdirSync(logsDir, { recursive: true });  // called on EVERY log line
  appendFileSync(entry.path, entry.line);
};
```

**Why it matters**: This is a synchronous filesystem syscall on every log write. While `mkdirSync` with `recursive: true` on an existing directory is cheap (it's essentially a stat+noop), it's still a syscall that blocks the event loop. In a busy session with heavy debug logging, this adds up. More importantly, it's unnecessary — the directory is already created in `enableFileLogging` (line 43).

**Suggested action**: Remove the `mkdirSync` call from `writeFileLog`. The directory is guaranteed to exist because:
1. `enableFileLogging` creates it on line 43 before flushing buffered entries
2. `writeFileLog` is only called after `isFileLoggingEnabled = true` (the guard on line 80 returns early otherwise)

If paranoia about directory deletion is desired, move the mkdir to a daily rotation point (when the log path changes), not on every write.

**Risk**: Very low — `enableFileLogging` already creates the directory. Removing the redundant call just eliminates waste. Edge case: if something external deletes the logs dir mid-session, `appendFileSync` will throw but the catch on line 87-88 already handles that gracefully.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

title: exportSession fetches session messages twice — redundant API call
description:
## Double fetch: getSessionMessages called twice in exportSession

**File path**: `src/service/session-export-service.ts` (lines 144-147)

**What**: `exportSession` runs `getSessionMessages(sessionID)` and `getTokenSummary(sessionID)` in parallel via `Promise.all`. But `getTokenSummary` (line 94) internally calls `getSessionMessages(sessionID)` again. So session messages are fetched **twice** for every export — once directly, once indirectly through `getTokenSummary`.

**Why it matters**: This is a wasted API round-trip on every session export. For large sessions with many messages, this doubles the data transfer and wait time. It's also the kind of bug that's invisible until someone profiles it — the comment on line 143 ('Fetch all data in parallel') actively masks the waste by making it look intentional.

**Suggested action**: Extract the token-computation logic from `getTokenSummary` into a pure helper `computeTokenSummary(messages: unknown[]): TokenSummary` that takes already-fetched messages. Then `exportSession` passes its own `messages` result into it:

```typescript
const [session, messages, diffs] = await Promise.all([...]);
const tokenSummary = this.computeTokenSummary(messages);
```

Keep the existing `getTokenSummary(sessionID)` as a public convenience wrapper that fetches + computes.

**Risk**: Low — the public API of `getTokenSummary` doesn't change. Internal refactor only.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

title: Consolidate beads directory detection — BeadsDetector duplicates ProjectDetectorService
description:
## Overlapping responsibility: `.beads/` directory detection in two places

**File paths**:
- `src/beads/detector.ts` — `BeadsDetector.detectBeadsDirectory()` (uses `accessSync`)
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts` — `ProjectDetectorService.detectBeadsInitialized()` (uses `fs.accessSync`)
- `src/service/beads-service.ts` — instantiates `BeadsDetector` in constructor AND again in `checkBeadsAvailability()`

**Description**: `.beads/` directory detection is implemented twice with identical logic:
1. `BeadsDetector.detectBeadsDirectory()` — exists solely to check for `.beads/`
2. `ProjectDetectorService.detectBeadsInitialized()` — does the same check

Additionally, `BeadsService` creates a `BeadsDetector` in its constructor (to set `this.beadsEnabled`) and then creates a *second* `BeadsDetector` instance in `checkBeadsAvailability()` (line 83) — redundant instantiation.

**Why it matters**: Two independent code paths checking the same filesystem state can drift apart. The `BeadsDetector` class (19 lines of detection logic) adds a whole class + options interface + export for something that's a single `fs.accessSync` call.

**Suggested action**: 
- Option A: Remove `BeadsDetector` entirely; `BeadsService` can inline the single `accessSync` check or delegate to `ProjectDetectorService`.
- Option B: Keep `BeadsDetector` but have `ProjectDetectorService` use it instead of reimplementing.
- Either way, fix the double-instantiation in `BeadsService`.

**Risk**: Low — both implementations are trivially equivalent today. Risk is in *not* consolidating (future drift).

**Safe to auto-apply**: User should decide between Option A vs B first.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

title: Fix import-from-internal-file violations per CODING.md conventions
description:
## Convention violation: imports from internal package files instead of package index

**File paths** (violators):
- `src/service/aimgr-service.ts:2` — `import type { Logger } from "../core/logger"`
- `src/service/beads-service.ts:2` — `import type { Logger } from "../core/logger"`
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts:5` — `import type { Logger } from "../core/logger"`
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts:6` — `import type { VersionInfo } from "../core/version"`
- `src/beads/detector.ts:3` — `import type { Logger } from "../core/logger"`
- `src/tool/coder-tool.ts:4` — `import type { SessionExportService } from "../service/session-export-service"`
- `src/tool/coder-tool.ts:5` — `import type { VersionInfo } from "../core/version"`
- `src/index.ts:6` — `import type { ProjectContext } from "./service/project-detector-service"`

**Convention (docs/CODING.md Section 2)**:
> Import from package index, not internal files: `import { Logger } from "./core"` ✅
> Never import from internal files: `import { Logger } from "./core/logger"` ❌

**Why it matters**: The project explicitly documents this convention to maintain encapsulation. Breaking it in 8 places undermines the package index pattern — internal file renames or reorganizations would cause cascading import fixes.

**Suggested action**: Change all violating imports to use the package index paths (`"../core"`, `"../service"`). `ProjectContext` is already exported from `src/service/index.ts`, so that fix is trivial.

**Risk**: None — type-only imports, no runtime behavior change.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.

title: Deduplicate  logic between AimgrService and ProjectDetectorService
description:
## Duplicated logic: aimgr verify result health check

**File paths**:
- `src/service/aimgr-service.ts` (lines 219-228 — `hasResourceIssues` method)
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts` (lines 313-317 — inline `hasIssues` in `detectResourcesHealthy`)

**Description**: Both files contain identical logic to determine whether an aimgr verify JSON result has issues:
```typescript
(Array.isArray(result.issues) && result.issues.length > 0) ||
(Array.isArray(result.errors) && result.errors.length > 0) ||
(result.error && result.error !== "") ||
(result.status && result.status !== "ok" && result.status !== "healthy")
```

`AimgrService` has it as `private hasResourceIssues(result)`, `ProjectDetectorService` has it as an inline expression.

**Why it matters**: If the aimgr verify JSON format changes (new field, renamed field), you must update both. This is a subtle divergence risk — one could be patched while the other is missed, causing different health assessments from the same data.

**Suggested action**: Extract to a shared `hasResourceIssues(result: unknown): boolean` pure function in `src/core/` and use it in both services. This is a natural companion to the `isExecTimeoutError` extraction.

**Risk**: Very low — pure function, no side effects, same logic in both locations today.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

title: Extract shared  helper to eliminate duplication
description:
## Duplicated method: `showToast`

**File paths**:
- `src/service/aimgr-service.ts` (lines 291-307)
- `src/service/beads-service.ts` (lines 147-163)
- `src/index.ts` (line 180 — inline `(client as any).tui.showToast(...)`)

**Description**: `AimgrService` and `BeadsService` each have an identical `private async showToast(...)` method that wraps `(this.client as any).tui.showToast(...)` with a try/catch and error log. `src/index.ts` has a third inline copy of the same pattern.

All three implementations:
1. Accept the same `{ title, message, variant, duration }` shape
2. Cast `client` to `any` to access `tui.showToast`
3. Catch errors and log them

**Why it matters**: Triplicated unsafe type-cast (`as any`) scattered across files. When the OpenCode SDK eventually types `tui.showToast`, you'll need to find and update three call sites instead of one.

**Suggested action**: Create a `showToast(client, logger, options)` free function in `src/core/` (or a thin `NotificationService`). All three consumers call that single function.

**Risk**: Low — the function is async but side-effect-only (fire-and-forget toast). Extract is straightforward.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes, but user should decide on placement (core helper vs. thin service class).

title: Extract shared  helper into

2. Do not log `"Beads CLI not installed"` for timeout cases
3. Do not show the install-this-binary toast for timeout cases
4. Preserve safe fallback behavior (no throw / degraded behavior)
5. Update tests to cover the corrected timeout-specific behavior

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A timeout in the bd CLI availability check is not labeled as missing installation
- [ ] Timeout-specific logging remains clear and includes command context
- [ ] Fallback behavior remains non-throwing / degraded
- [ ] Tests cover the corrected timeout behavior in `BeadsService`

## Problem
The startup-timeout hardening work in opencode-coder-jlp added timeouts to all targeted `execSync` calls, but several timeout paths still do not log a clear timeout-specific message. Some command-check paths treat a timeout like a simple missing binary, and one path suppresses the underlying error entirely. This leaves an acceptance gap against the requirement that timeout errors be caught and logged clearly.

## Evidence
Post-implementation verification found these timeout paths:
- `src/service/aimgr-service.ts` → `isAimgrAvailable()` catches all errors and logs `"aimgr CLI not found on PATH"`, which is misleading for timeout failures
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts` → `detectBdCliInstalled()` and `detectAimgrInstalled()` log `not found on PATH` on timeout
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts` → `detectCoderPackageInstalled()` catches all errors and logs only `Could not detect opencode-coder package via aimgr list`, without the timeout cause
- `src/service/beads-service.ts` → `isBdCliInstalled()` returns `false` with no timeout-specific log; the caller later warns that beads CLI is not installed

## Required fix
1. Preserve existing fallback return values (`false`/`null`) for timeout failures
2. Add clear timeout-aware logging that identifies the command that timed out
3. Avoid misleading `not found on PATH` messages for timeout cases
4. Add tests covering timeout handling for the affected command-check paths

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Startup command-check timeout paths log clear timeout-specific messages
- [ ] Fallback behavior remains unchanged (`false`/`null` as before)
- [ ] No timeout path is logged as a misleading missing-binary condition
- [ ] Tests cover the affected timeout/logging paths

title: Startup aimgr health check ignores orphan warnings from repo-local .opencode resources
description:
## Description
In this repository, `aimgr verify --format json` returns orphan warnings for repo-local development resources under `.opencode/`. Plugin startup logs the warnings but still reports `resourcesHealthy=true` and `ecosystemReady=true`.

## Component
`AimgrService` / startup health evaluation for aimgr resource verification.

## Expected Behavior
If `aimgr verify` reports orphaned resources, startup health should either:
- treat that result as unhealthy and surface actionable guidance, or
- intentionally exclude repo-local `.opencode/` development resources from verification.

The readiness state written to `.coder/project.yaml` should match the actual verify result.

## Actual Behavior
`aimgr verify --format json` returns a warning array:
- `skill-validator` installed under `.opencode/skills/skill-validator`
- `skill-tester-agent` installed under `.opencode/agents/skill-tester-agent`

Despite that, startup logs:
- `resourcesHealthy=true`
- `repairAttempted=false`
- `ecosystemReady=true`

This means the startup health check is overstating readiness in the presence of real verify warnings.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `aimgr verify --format json` in this repository.
2. Observe orphan warnings for `skill-validator` and `skill-tester-agent` under `.opencode/`.
3. Start `opencode serve --print-logs --log-level DEBUG` and trigger `/agent`.
4. Observe startup logs include the warning payload while still reporting `resourcesHealthy=true` and `ecosystemReady=true`.

## Evidence
- Independently re-verified on 2026-03-15.
- Direct command output in this repo returns the orphan warning array.
- Startup reproduction log: `/tmp/opencode-retention.log:85-98`
- Current local resources present:
  - `.opencode/skills/skill-validator/`
  - `.opencode/agents/skill-tester-agent.md`
- `ai.package.yaml` does not declare either resource.

## Environment
- opencode 1.2.26
- aimgr 3.3.0
- bd 0.59.0
- Linux

## Impact
- Every startup in this repo emits noisy aimgr warnings.
- Startup health reporting is inaccurate.
- Automatic repair is skipped even though verify reported issues.
- `.coder/project.yaml` and default-agent gating can present the repo as fully healthy when it is not.

## Suspected Cause
`src/service/aimgr-service.ts` currently treats verify output as an object shape (`issues`, `errors`, `status`). In this case `aimgr verify --format json` returns an array of warning objects, so `hasResourceIssues()` incorrectly treats the result as healthy.

## Relevant Files
- `src/service/aimgr-service.ts`
- `src/index.ts`
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts`
- `ai.package.yaml`

title: Cleanup Release Tasks
description:
## Cleanup: Mark release tasks for compaction

Close the epic and mark all tasks with label for future compaction.

### Steps
```bash
# Close the epic
bd update $PARENT --status=closed

# Mark epic and all tasks for compaction
bd update $PARENT --add-label=marked-for-compaction
for task_id in $QUALITY $DOCS $BUMP $RELEASE $NOTES $VERIFY; do
  bd update $task_id --add-label=marked-for-compaction
done

# Mark cleanup task itself
```

title: Automatically run aimgr repair when verify finds fixable resource issues
description:
## Description
As a startup resilience feature, the plugin should automatically attempt `aimgr repair` when `aimgr verify --format json` reports fixable resource issues.

This feature is independent of the stale-readiness/config-hook bug fixed in `opencode-coder-7rn`. Its purpose is to reduce manual setup friction by repairing recoverable aimgr resource problems automatically.

## Expected Behavior
When `aimgr verify` reports repairable resource issues during startup, the plugin should:
1. attempt `aimgr repair --format json`
2. run verification again
3. use the post-repair result as the authoritative resource health state
4. inform the user whether auto-repair was attempted and whether it succeeded

## Suggested Implementation
1. Run `aimgr verify --format json` during startup
2. If issues are found and aimgr is available, run `aimgr repair --format json` automatically
3. Re-run verification after repair
4. Update readiness state based on the post-repair verification result
5. Show user feedback for repair attempted / repair succeeded / repair failed

## Files to Modify
- `src/service/aimgr-service.ts` — add repair-and-reverify flow
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts` — consume repaired health state for readiness
- `src/index.ts` — orchestrate startup behavior and user notification
- related tests under `tests/unit/` and integration coverage where needed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The plugin automatically attempts `aimgr repair` when `aimgr verify` reports fixable issues
- [ ] Verification is run again after repair
- [ ] Project readiness reflects the post-repair verification state
- [ ] The user is informed when automatic repair is attempted and whether it succeeded
- [ ] Tests cover verify-fails -> repair-succeeds and verify-fails -> repair-fails flows
close_reason: Implemented startup verify→auto-repair→re-verify flow with authoritative post-repair health for readiness; added user feedback and unit/integration coverage for healthy, repaired, and unrepaired paths.

title: Show user feedback when ecosystem readiness blocks orchestrator default
description:
## Description
When the plugin correctly determines that `default_agent=orchestrator` is not being set because project ecosystem readiness is not satisfied, the user should receive clear feedback in the UI explaining why orchestration was skipped.

## Scope
This issue is limited to user-facing feedback for the genuine `ecosystemReady=false` branch. It does not implement auto-repair.

## Expected Behavior
If the plugin skips setting orchestrator as the default agent because the project is not fully ready yet, it should show a warning toast with a plain-language explanation and a concise next step.

## Implemented Behavior
- Show a warning toast only when:
  - no `default_agent` is already configured
  - `projectContext` exists
  - `projectContext.ecosystemReady === false`
- The toast explains that orchestrator was not enabled because the project is not fully ready yet
- The toast points users to aimgr/beads setup and `/opencode-coder/doctor`
- No toast is shown for:
  - existing configured default agent
  - unavailable project context
  - successful orchestrator assignment

## Files Modified
- `src/index.ts`
- `tests/helpers/mock-client.ts`
- `tests/integration/plugin.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A user-visible notification is shown when orchestrator is not selected due to readiness failure
- [x] The notification explains the primary reason in plain language
- [x] The reason is also logged for debugging
- [x] Tests cover the branch where readiness is false and orchestrator is skipped
close_reason: Added warning toast for the genuine ecosystemReady=false branch so users get plain-language feedback when orchestrator is not made the default agent. Added integration coverage to verify toast is shown only for the not-ready case and not for other skip paths.

description:
## Create GitHub Release

Create the v0.33.0 release using the repository's `release.yml` workflow.

### Preconditions
- `opencode-coder-wwt.2` already pushed the release-prep changelog/docs commit to `origin/main`.
- `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` should match before dispatch.
- `release-notes.md` is intentionally local-only and is passed as workflow input; it does not need to be committed.

### Preferred Method: GitHub Actions Workflow
```bash
git rev-parse HEAD
git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main
jq -n --arg version "0.33.0" --rawfile notes release-notes.md '{version:$version, release_notes:$notes}'   | gh workflow run release.yml --ref main --json

```

### Verification

title: aimgr bootstrap warns about missing git author identity in isolated launcher env
description:
## Discovered in
Manual Phase 1 bootstrap validation for `opencode-coder-bwrr` using the isolated `empty-project` launcher environment on 2026-04-18.

## Expected
Fresh isolated bootstrap should either avoid git-identity-dependent commit steps or present a clean success path without confusing author-identity warnings.

## Actual
`aimgr repo add` / `aimgr repo apply-manifest` / `aimgr repo sync` succeeded, but also emitted warnings that git author identity was unknown (for example `fatal: unable to auto-detect email address`).

## Repro
1. Create a fresh isolated launcher workspace with `bun run test:manual -- --mode=shell --fixture=empty-project`.
2. In that preserved environment, run either the public apply-manifest flow or a local-source fallback (`aimgr repo add` or `aimgr repo apply-manifest`, then `aimgr repo sync`).
3. Observe the output.

## Impact
This is non-blocking, but it adds confusing noise to the first-run bootstrap path and may make users think setup failed even when it succeeded.

## Evidence
- Manual launcher artifacts: `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder/.manual-test-runs/run-PnUQEF`, `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder/.manual-test-runs/run-YjR1ts`, `/home/hans/dev/github/opencode-coder/.manual-test-runs/run-FHVtcp`
close_reason: Could not reproduce on 2026-04-19; isolated launcher env now seeds git author/committer identity and aimgr bootstrap completed without warning.

title: Unify OPENCODE_CODER_DEBUG parsing across logger and coder tool
description:
## Description
The simplify pass fixed `coder plugin` to use the canonical disabled-state helper, but debug-state reporting is still inconsistent across the codebase. `src/core/logger.ts` enables debug logging for any truthy `OPENCODE_CODER_DEBUG` value, while `src/tool/coder-tool.ts` reports debug enabled only when the value is exactly `"1"`.

## Instructions
1. Add a canonical helper for `OPENCODE_CODER_DEBUG` parsing in `src/config/env.ts`.
2. Export that helper from `src/config/index.ts`.
3. Update `src/core/logger.ts` and `src/tool/coder-tool.ts` to use the shared helper.
4. Keep behavior explicit and documented so the logger and `coder plugin` report the same state.
5. Add or update focused unit coverage for the helper behavior.

## Files to Modify
- src/config/env.ts — add shared debug helper
- src/config/index.ts — export helper
- src/core/logger.ts — use shared helper
- src/tool/coder-tool.ts — use shared helper
- tests/unit/env.test.ts — add helper coverage
- tests/unit/logger.test.ts — update or extend coverage if needed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Logger and `coder plugin` use the same debug-state helper
- [ ] `coder plugin` reports the same debug state the logger actually uses
- [ ] Focused unit tests cover the chosen parsing behavior
- [ ] `bun test tests/unit/env.test.ts tests/unit/logger.test.ts` passes
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

title: coder-tool.ts uses dynamic imports for node builtins that are already available
description:
## Unnecessary dynamic imports: `await import('node:fs')` etc. in coder-tool.ts

**File paths**:
- `src/tool/coder-tool.ts:99-100` — `beads` sub-command: `await import("node:fs")`, `await import("node:path")`
- `src/tool/coder-tool.ts:137-139` — `logs` sub-command: `await import("node:os")`, `await import("node:fs")`, `await import("node:path")`

**Description**: The `beads` and `logs` sub-commands use `await import(...)` for `node:fs`, `node:path`, and `node:os`. These are Node/Bun builtins that are always available and have zero load cost. The file already has a static `import { isAbsolute, join } from "node:path"` at line 3.

Dynamic imports are useful for optional dependencies or code-splitting, but Node builtins are neither — they're always present and already loaded by the runtime.

**Why it matters**: 
1. **Readability**: Each sub-command block starts with 2-3 dynamic import lines that add visual noise.
2. **Inconsistency**: `node:path` is imported statically at the top AND dynamically in two sub-commands.
3. **Unnecessary async overhead**: Each `await import()` creates a microtask for a module that's already cached.

**Suggested action**: Replace the dynamic imports with static imports at the top of the file:
```typescript
import * as fs from "node:fs";
import * as path from "node:path";
import * as os from "node:os";
```

Then remove the `await import()` lines from the sub-command blocks.

**Risk**: None — these are built-in modules, always available.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

title: ProjectDetectorService.detectAndWrite is async but contains no await
description:
## Unnecessary async: detectAndWrite is purely synchronous

**File path**: `src/service/project-detector-service.ts:421`

**Description**: `detectAndWrite` is declared `async` and returns `Promise<ProjectContext>`, but the entire method body is synchronous — no `await` expressions, no promise chains, no async calls. Every detection method it calls (`detectGitInitialized`, `detectBeadsInitialized`, `detectBdCliInstalled`, etc.) is synchronous. `writeProjectContext` is synchronous.

The `async` keyword was likely added for future-proofing or because the callers expected a promise, but as written it just wraps a synchronous return value in an unnecessary Promise.

**Why it matters**: 
1. **Misleading API**: Callers treat this as an async operation and add `.then()/.catch()` chains (see `src/index.ts:60-90`), but nothing actually yields. This hides the fact that all work is blocking on the event loop during `execSync` calls.
2. **Minor overhead**: Unnecessary microtask scheduling for a pure-sync operation.

**Suggested action**: 
- Option A: Keep `async` signature (for future-proofing) but add a comment explaining the sync nature. Low-priority.
- Option B: Remove `async`, change return type to `ProjectContext`, update callers. More honest but requires caller changes.

This is a code smell, not a bug. The method works correctly either way.

**Risk**: None behaviorally. Option B requires changing the promise chain in `src/index.ts`.

**Safe to auto-apply**: User should decide between A and B.
close_reason: Removed synchronous detectAndWrite async wrapper, updated callers, tests, and docs

title: beads/index.ts comment contradicts its own export statement
description:
## Misleading comment: says 'not exported publicly' while exporting publicly

**File path**: `src/beads/index.ts`

**Description**: Line 1 says:
```typescript
// BeadsDetector is internal to BeadsService, not exported publicly
export { BeadsDetector, type BeadsDetectorOptions } from "./detector";
```

The comment claims BeadsDetector is 'not exported publicly', but the very next line `export`s it. This is the package's public index file — anything exported here IS the public API.

**Why it matters**: A developer reading this file will be confused: is BeadsDetector intended to be internal or public? If it's internal, the export should be removed (and `BeadsService` should import directly from `./detector`). If it's public, the comment is wrong. Either way, the current state is contradictory.

This also relates to existing issue opencode-coder-u8e (consolidating BeadsDetector). If Option A (remove BeadsDetector) is chosen, this file becomes empty or can be removed. If Option B is chosen, the comment should be deleted.

**Suggested action**: Remove the misleading comment. The export speaks for itself. (Or, if BeadsDetector is truly internal-only, remove the export and have BeadsService import directly.)

**Risk**: None — comment-only change.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

title: Duplicate  CLI availability pattern — extract shared helper
description:
## Duplicated pattern: `command -v <tool>` CLI availability checks

**File paths**:
- `src/service/aimgr-service.ts:62-82` — `isAimgrAvailable()` checks `command -v aimgr`
- `src/service/beads-service.ts:123-142` — `getBdCliAvailability()` checks `command -v bd`
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts:194-215` — `detectBdCliInstalled()` checks `command -v bd`
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts:224-245` — `detectAimgrInstalled()` checks `command -v aimgr`

**Description**: Four methods across three files all run `execSync("command -v <name>", { stdio: "ignore", timeout: COMMAND_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS })` with the same timeout-error handling pattern. The structure is identical — only the CLI name differs.

**Why it matters**: Four copies of the same try/catch/timeout-check pattern. If Node/Bun changes exec error semantics or you want to add caching (avoid re-shelling out for `command -v aimgr` multiple times in the same startup), four places need changing.

**Suggested action**: Extract a `isCommandAvailable(name: string, logger: Logger, timeoutMs?: number): boolean` helper into `src/core/exec.ts`. All four call sites become one-liners.

This naturally bundles with the `isExecTimeoutError` and timeout constant extractions.

**Risk**: Very low — pure function wrapping execSync.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.
close_reason: Implemented in simplify pass

title: Extract shared timeout constants to a single location
description:
## Duplicated constants: `COMMAND_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` and `AIMGR_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`

- `src/service/aimgr-service.ts` (lines 9-10)
- `src/service/beads-service.ts` (line 8)
- `src/service/project-detector-service.ts` (lines 8-9)

**Description**: `COMMAND_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000` is defined in all three files. `AIMGR_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000` is defined in both `aimgr-service.ts` and `project-detector-service.ts`.

**Why it matters**: If you need to tune timeouts (e.g., slow CI environments), you'd need to find and update multiple files. These should be single-source-of-truth constants.

**Suggested action**: Define both constants in `src/core/exec.ts` (same file as the `isExecTimeoutError` extraction) and import them where needed. Alternatively put in a `src/core/constants.ts`.

**Risk**: None — numeric constants, zero behavioral change.

**Safe to auto-apply**: Yes.

title: Concurrent `opencode serve` bootstrap emits snapshot cleanup GC warning
description:
## Description
Starting two `opencode serve` processes against the same repository and triggering bootstrap on both via `/agent` can emit a snapshot cleanup warning during startup.

## Component
OpenCode snapshot cleanup during concurrent repository bootstrap (likely upstream OpenCode, not plugin logic).

## Expected Behavior
Concurrent startups against the same repository should either serialize snapshot GC, retry safely, or log a clearly benign message without a fatal Git warning.

## Actual Behavior
One of the concurrent server processes logs:
- `service=snapshot exitCode=128 stderr=fatal: gc is already running ...`
- `stdout= cleanup failed`

The request still completes successfully, so the main symptom is noisy/fatal-looking startup output during concurrent bootstrap.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start two `opencode serve --print-logs --log-level DEBUG` processes against this repository on different ports.
2. Trigger bootstrap on both instances with concurrent `GET /agent` requests.
3. Observe one process log the `service=snapshot ... cleanup failed` warning during startup.

## Evidence
- Independently re-verified on 2026-03-15 with `opencode 1.2.26`.
- Reproduction log: `/tmp/opencode-concurrency-check-2/serve1.log:198-199`
- Original verification log: `/tmp/opencode-verify-2.log:198-199`

## Environment
- opencode 1.2.26
- aimgr 3.3.0
- bd 0.59.0
- Linux

## Impact
- Does not appear to break startup or the `/agent` request.
- Produces fatal-looking noise during concurrent startup verification.
- Can mislead debugging of multi-process OpenCode behavior.

## Notes
- Reproduced without changing repository code.
- This currently looks like an upstream OpenCode concurrency issue rather than an `opencode-coder` implementation bug.
close_reason: Verified as an upstream OpenCode concurrency warning, not an opencode-coder bug

title: Release verification install example breaks transitive dependency resolution by forcing global GitHub Packages registry
description:
## Problem
The release verification documentation uses an installation command that forces **all** package resolution through GitHub Packages:

```bash
npm install --no-save @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0 --registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
```

Because the command uses a global `--registry` override, npm resolves transitive dependencies such as `@opencode-ai/plugin` from GitHub Packages instead of npmjs. That breaks installation even when the published package itself is valid.

## Expected Behavior
The release verification install example should validate that `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder` can be installed from GitHub Packages **without** redirecting public transitive dependencies to the wrong registry.

A clean verification flow should:
- fetch `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder` from `https://npm.pkg.github.com`
- continue resolving public dependencies from the default npm registry
- succeed in a clean temp directory when valid authentication is present

## Actual Behavior
In a clean temp directory, the documented install flow fails with `npm ERR! code E404` because npm requests the public dependency `@opencode-ai/plugin` from GitHub Packages:

```text
npm error 404 Not Found - GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@opencode-ai%2fplugin
npm error 404 The requested resource '@opencode-ai/plugin@^1.2.16' could not be found or you do not have permission to access it.
```

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a clean temp directory
2. Add scoped registry configuration only for `@dynatrace-oss`:
   ```bash
   printf '@dynatrace-oss:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n' > .npmrc
   ```
3. Run the documented release verification install command:
   ```bash
   npm install --no-save @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0 --registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
   ```
4. Observe npm attempting to download `@opencode-ai/plugin` from GitHub Packages and failing with `E404`

## Environment
- **Operating System**: Linux
- **Node.js Version**: v24.14.0
- **npm Version**: 11.9.0
- **bd CLI Version**: 0.59.0
- **Plugin Version under verification**: `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0`
- **Shell**: bash

## Evidence
Reproduced locally on 2026-03-12 using the documented verification flow.

Broken command:
```bash
printf '@dynatrace-oss:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n' > .npmrc
npm install --no-save @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0 --registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
```

Working comparison:
```bash
printf '@dynatrace-oss:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n' > .npmrc
npm install --no-save @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0
```

The working comparison confirms that the package publication itself is fine; the failure is caused by the verification example.

## Root Cause Analysis
The global `--registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` flag overrides registry resolution for **all** packages in the install graph, not just the top-level `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder` package.

That causes npm to fetch public transitive dependencies from GitHub Packages, where they do not exist. The example therefore tests the wrong thing and produces a false failure.

## Affected Documentation / Files
- `docs/RELEASING.md` — the post-release `npm install` verification example only
- any release checklist/task text copied from the same `npm install ... --registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` example

## Recommended Fix Direction
1. Remove the global `--registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` flag from the `npm install` verification example
2. Keep only the scoped registry mapping in `.npmrc` for `@dynatrace-oss`
3. Leave metadata verification commands such as `npm view ... --registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` unchanged
4. Update release verification guidance so public dependencies continue resolving from npmjs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/RELEASING.md` no longer uses a global `--registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` override in the post-release `npm install` example
- [ ] The `npm view ... --registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` metadata verification example remains unchanged
- [ ] The documented install example uses scoped `.npmrc` configuration plus a plain `npm install`
- [ ] Verification guidance no longer causes public transitive dependencies to be fetched from the wrong registry
close_reason: Updated the post-release install verification example in docs/RELEASING.md to use scoped .npmrc registry configuration and plain npm install, preventing public transitive dependencies from being routed to GitHub Packages. Left npm view metadata verification unchanged.

title: Found: render_eval_review does not escape </script> in eval data
description: Discovered while verifying opencode-coder-hly. title: Release verification gh auth token flow fails for GitHub Packages because active token lacks package-read scope
description:
## Problem
The release verification/authentication guidance assumes that `gh auth token` can be used directly as the npm authentication token for reading `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder` from GitHub Packages.

In the current environment, that assumption is false: the active GitHub CLI token does not include the required package-read scope, so npm access to GitHub Packages fails even though the package is published correctly.

## Expected Behavior
If the documentation recommends using `gh auth token` for GitHub Packages verification, that flow should succeed with the documented prerequisites.

If additional token scopes are required, the documentation should say so explicitly and provide a working verification method.

## Actual Behavior
Using the active `gh auth token` in `.npmrc` causes package install from GitHub Packages to fail with `npm ERR! code E403`:

```text
npm error 403 Forbidden - GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@dynatrace-oss%2fopencode-coder
npm error 403 Permission permission_denied: The token provided does not match expected scopes.
```

At the same time:
- `npm view @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0 --registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` succeeds
- a scoped install using existing working npm auth succeeds

That confirms the package exists and publication succeeded; the failure is specific to the `gh auth token` npm auth flow.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Confirm GitHub CLI auth status:
   ```bash
   gh auth status
   ```
2. Observe that the active token scopes do **not** include `read:packages`
3. Create a clean temp directory and write `.npmrc` using the active GitHub CLI token:
   ```bash
   TOKEN=$(gh auth token)
   printf '@dynatrace-oss:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=%s\n' "$TOKEN" > .npmrc
   ```
4. Attempt package installation:
   ```bash
   npm install --no-save @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0
   ```
5. Observe `E403 permission_denied` from GitHub Packages

## Environment
- **Operating System**: Linux
- **Node.js Version**: v24.14.0
- **npm Version**: 11.9.0
- **bd CLI Version**: 0.59.0
- **Package under verification**: `@dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0`
- **Shell**: bash
- **Active gh token scopes**: `gist`, `read:org`, `repo`, `workflow` (no `read:packages`)

## Evidence
Reproduced locally on 2026-03-12.

Broken auth flow:
```bash
TOKEN=$(gh auth token)
printf '@dynatrace-oss:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=%s\n' "$TOKEN" > .npmrc
npm install --no-save @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0
```

Observed failure:
```text
npm error 403 Permission permission_denied: The token provided does not match expected scopes.
```

Working comparison:
```bash
printf '@dynatrace-oss:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n' > .npmrc
npm install --no-save @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@0.33.0
```

The working comparison confirms publication is healthy and the broken part is the token-based authentication guidance.

## Root Cause Analysis
The documented `gh auth token` verification path assumes the active GitHub CLI token is authorized for GitHub Packages reads.

In this environment, the active token lacks the required package-read scope, so GitHub Packages rejects the request with `permission_denied`.

This is separate from `opencode-coder-isp`:
- `opencode-coder-isp` = wrong registry routing breaks transitive dependencies
- `opencode-coder-eb3` = the `gh auth token`-based auth method is not valid unless the token has package-read scope

## Affected Documentation / Flows
- release verification notes/tasks that recommend using `gh auth token` for npm auth
- troubleshooting guidance that implies `gh auth login` is sufficient for GitHub Packages verification
- any automation or manual verification flow that assumes `gh auth token` always grants package-read access

## Recommended Fix Direction
1. Update release/auth documentation to explicitly require a token with GitHub Packages read scope (for example `read:packages`)
2. Do not imply that `gh auth token` is universally sufficient for npm verification
3. Provide a known-good verification method using either:
   - a PAT/token with package-read scope, or
   - an existing npm auth configuration already known to work
4. Separate package existence verification from package-auth verification in release docs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Documentation explicitly states the token scope requirements for GitHub Packages npm verification
- [ ] The recommended auth flow succeeds in a clean temp directory when the documented prerequisites are met
- [ ] Release verification guidance distinguishes package publication success from auth misconfiguration/scope failures
- [ ] The docs no longer imply that any active `gh auth token` is sufficient for GitHub Packages reads
close_reason: Updated release docs to require read:packages-capable npm token, clarified metadata-vs-auth verification distinction, and removed implication that any gh auth token works
